greatrwandajobs.title: Customer Care Officer job at Kungahara SACCO Ruhango
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background

KUNGAHARA SACCO RUHANGO (K.S.R) is a District Savings and Credit Cooperative (D-SACCO) established following the consolidation of Nine Umurenge Sacco’s operating within RUHANGO District, in accordance with the Government of Rwanda SACCO consolidation framework. K.S.R is duly registered under RCA and licensed by the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR).

In accordance with the Government of Rwanda SACCO’s consolidation framework and under the supervision of the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) KUNGAHARA SACCO RUHANGO is looking for qualified, competent, committed, proactive and self-motivated individual to fill the following positions:

Position Name: Customer Care Officer (branch)

Reports to: Branch Business Manager

Supervision: Under the supervision and guidance of the Branch Business Officer with reporting line to the Branch Business Manager

Responsibilities & Tasks

Under the supervision and guidance of the Branch Business Officer with Reporting line to the Branch Business Manager:

  • To work diligently on the assigned work on time and to produce results;
  • To comply with the instructions of the employer or his/her representative;
  • To take good care of and manage the equipment assigned to him/her in his/her work;
  • To be at work and respect working days and hours;
  • Files documents of the SACCO, e.g., member documents;
  • Initiates and updates all documents related to member’s information (e.g., electronic customer file, membership applications, authorizations, customer notes);
  • To provide good and efficient service to customers;
  • To follow up on customer complaints that have been referred to other appropriate authorities;
  • Assist in resolving daily customer issues and ensure that they are timely responded in accordance with established customer service policies and regulations;
  • Maintain knowledge of all products and services offered by the Cooperative and provide information on the Cooperative's products and activities to members and customers in general;
  • Receive and assist members and customers in general who require services related to deposits and withdrawals and ensure the security of related documents;
  • Ensure that the information recorded in the member's passbook matches with his/her account in the electronic system;
  • Collect and report on unresolved customer complaints or issues and requests for follow-up, documentation and submission to the relevant authority for consideration;
  • Assist in the implementation of the Cooperative's policies, procedures and guidelines for customer care;
  • Participate in the implementation of the customer care policy and in particular the protection of financial services consumers;
  • Inform and explain to members and customers information regarding the contents of their accounts;
  • Assist customers in completing any documents that may be required;
  • Conduct Customer Satisfaction Surveys in accordance with the relevant regulations;
  • Open new accounts and ensure that their documents are submitted to the relevant department or employee for approval;
  • Maintain good relations with all customers, focusing on changes and new needs in the Cooperative;
  • Issue bank statements to members and customers after payment of the required fees;
  • To provide advice to members and clients in general by teaching them how to invest and maintain a culture of saving;
  • To perform other duties that do not conflict with the laws and regulations required by the supervisor or his/her superior authority.

  • At least secondary education (A2) in Accounting, Finance or in related domain.
  • Excellent service orientation and attention to details regarding the atmosphere in the SACCO.
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Two years’ experience in customer care services.
  • Excellent multi-tasking skills and be able to function under pressure.
  • Excellent negotiation skills and be able to influence people.
  • Must be patient and willing to help others in solving problems while maintaining a positive attitude at all times.

greatrwandajobs.description:
1. ROLE SUMMARY

The Legal Officer supports the Head of Legal & Company Secretary in providing sound legal advice, drafting and reviewing corporate documents, and managing legal risks to protect the commercial and regulatory interests of Ecofleet Solutions Ltd.

2. SCOPE OF THE ROLE

The role involves supporting corporate governance, contract management, regulatory compliance, and litigation processes. The Legal Officer works closely with internal departments and external counsel, reporting directly to the Head of Legal & Company Secretary.

3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Draft, review, and negotiate commercial contracts, agreements, and MOUs.
  • Provide legal opinions on labor law, commercial transactions, and intellectual property matters.
  • Maintain statutory records and ensure timely corporate filings with RDB and relevant authorities.
  • Coordinate with external counsel on litigation and represent the company in administrative proceedings where required.
  • Review and update internal policies to ensure legal and regulatory compliance.
  • Identify and mitigate legal risks across company operations.

4. WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

The Legal Officer maintains the following key working relationships:

  • Head of Legal & Company Secretary: Direct reporting line; legal strategy and escalation of key legal matters.
  • Internal Departments: Legal advisory support on contracts, transactions, and compliance matters.
  • External Counsel: Coordination on litigation and specialised legal matters.
  • RDB & Regulatory Authorities: Corporate filings and regulatory compliance.

5. INDICATORS OF SUCCESS

  • Legal documents reviewed and returned within 48-72 hours.
  • Minimisation of legal exposure and successful out-of-court settlements.
  • 100% compliance with statutory filing deadlines.

greatrwandajobs.title: Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer job at Ecofleet Solutions Ltd
greatrwandajobs.description:
1. ROLE SUMMARY

The Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer drives data-driven decision-making and innovation across Ecofleet's operations and digital ecosystem. Reporting to the CDXO, the role focuses on transforming data into actionable insights, identifying opportunities for innovation, and supporting the continuous improvement of services, systems, and customer experience. The Officer plays a central role in analytics, reporting, and digital innovation, working across departments to unlock value from data and support strategic and operational performance.

2. SCOPE OF THE ROLE

The Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer develops and manages data analytics frameworks and reporting systems, analyzes operational, financial, and digital data to generate insights, and identifies and supports the implementation of digital innovation initiatives. The role builds dashboards and visualization tools for decision-making, supports predictive analytics and performance optimization efforts, and promotes a data-driven culture across the organization.

3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Collect, clean, and analyze data from multiple sources (FMS, finance systems, digital platforms, operations).
  • Develop and maintain dashboards and reports for operational and executive use.
  • Identify trends, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities across fleet operations and customer experience.
  • Support development of predictive models (e.g., demand forecasting, maintenance planning, route optimization).
  • Collaborate with the M&E Officer to align KPI tracking and reporting frameworks.
  • Work with the FMS Product Officer and Platform & UX Officer to enhance data availability and usability.
  • Explore and recommend innovative digital solutions (automation, AI, data tools) to improve performance.
  • Support pilot projects and innovation initiatives with data analysis and evaluation.
  • Ensure data quality, consistency, and governance across systems.
  • Present insights and recommendations to leadership in a clear and actionable manner.

4. WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

The Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer maintains the following key working relationships:

  • CDXO: Strategic direction on analytics and innovation priorities.
  • FMS Product Officer: Access to fleet data and system-based insights.
  • Platform & UX Officer: User behavior analytics and experience optimization.
  • Enterprise IT & Cybersecurity Officer: Data infrastructure, security, and governance.
  • M&E Officer: Alignment of KPIs, reporting standards, and performance frameworks.
  • COO: Operational insights and performance optimization.
  • CFO: Financial analytics and cost optimization.
  • CSEO: Sustainability metrics and environmental performance tracking.
  • Data & Analytics Solution Providers: Tools, platforms, and technical support.
  • Consultants, Research & Innovation Partners: Support on analytics and innovation initiatives.

5. INDICATORS OF SUCCESS

  • Availability of accurate, timely, and actionable analytics dashboards.
  • Increased use of data in operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Measurable improvements driven by data insights (efficiency, cost savings, service quality).
  • Successful implementation of innovation initiatives and pilots.
  • Strong alignment between analytics outputs and business needs.
  • Improved data quality and consistency across systems.

6. CORE COMPETENCIES & SKILLS

  • Strong analytical and data interpretation skills.
  • Proficiency in data tools (Excel, Power BI, SQL, or similar).
  • Understanding of data modeling, visualization, and reporting.
  • Ability to translate data into actionable insights.
  • Curiosity and innovation mindset.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills.
  • Attention to detail and data accuracy.

7. VALUES & CULTURAL FIT

  • Data-driven mindset and commitment to evidence-based decisions.
  • Curiosity and continuous improvement.
  • Collaboration across departments.
  • Accountability and ownership of insights and outcomes.
  • Passion for innovation in mobility and public service.

8. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum:

  • Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Economics, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field.
  • 3-5 years' experience in data analysis, analytics, or digital innovation roles.

Preferred:

  • Experience in transport, logistics, energy, or infrastructure sectors.
  • Strong skills in Power BI, SQL, Python, or similar tools.
  • Experience with predictive analytics or machine learning (basic to intermediate).
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders.
  • Exposure to digital transformation or innovation projects.

greatrwandajobs.description:
Notice for Provision of Cleaning Services for 2027 Tender at SNV Rwanda

About SNV and Background of the assignment

SNV SNV Netherlands Development Organization is a not-for-profit international development organization founded in the Netherlands in 1965 with a global presence in 30 countries across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. As an organization, SNV focuses on the Agriculture, WASH, and Energy sectors with the belief that no one should have to live in poverty and that all people should have the opportunity to pursue their own sustainable development. SNV contributes to these sectors by strengthening the capacity of targeted partners and communities at the field level to realize increased skill sets and sustainable performance; reduce poverty levels and expand employment; and improve food security while paying special attention to gender equity, social inclusion of marginalized groups and stakeholder accountability.

1.2. Background of the Assignment 

SNV Rwanda invites reputable and experienced companies to submit quotations for the provision of cleaning services. The selected service provider will provide cleaning services on an as-needed basis for a period of twelve (12) months, in accordance with the requirements and terms set out in this RFQ.

Offerors are responsible for ensuring that their quotations are submitted in accordance with the instructions, requirements, terms and conditions contained in this RFQ. Failure to comply with the requirements may result in the offer being considered non-responsive.

2. General Instructions and conditions

This is a Request for Quotations only. Issuance of this RFQ does not obligate SNV to make an award or reimburse any costs incurred by an offeror in preparing or submitting an offer.

  • Any award resulting from this RFQ will be formalised through an appropriate SNV contractual instrument.
  • SNV reserves the right to request clarifications or negotiate with any offeror before making an award.
  • SNV may make a partial award or split the award among more than one service provider where this is considered to be in SNV's best interest.
  • SNV reserves the right to cancel the RFQ at any time.
  • Payment will normally be made within thirty (30) calendar days after receipt of a valid invoice and confirmation that the services have been satisfactorily delivered and accepted.
  • Release of payment is subject to satisfactory performance and written acceptance of the services in accordance with the RFQ and the resulting contract or purchase order.

3. Terms of reference and Service requirements

SNV is seeking offers from reputable, well established and experienced offerors, duly incorporated under the Laws of Rwanda to provide cleaning services under a Fixed Contract Agreement (FCA), at fixed prices for a period of 12 months.

3.1 Responsibilities of offeror (Company, supplier or vendor)

  • The following cleaning instructions are outlined by building, cleaning location within the building and cleaning schedule.
  • Empty all waste receptacles, replace liners as required, and remove waste to the designated collection point. SNV will provide waste-bin liners.
  • Spot-clean partition glass to remove fingerprints, smudges and other marks.
  • Dust horizontal and vertical surfaces, including windowsills, ledges, mouldings, telephones, pictures, office furniture and other furnishings.
  • Clean drinking fountains, removing watermarks and splashes from surrounding surfaces.
  • Dust-mop all hard-surface floors.
  • Damp-mop hard-surface floors, including corners, edges and areas beneath furniture where accessible.
  • Spot-clean walls, light switches and doors to remove fingerprints, smudges and spills.
  • Clean interior windows and both sides of partition glass, including damp-wiping window and glass frames.
  • Clean and sanitise toilets and urinals inside and outside, including polishing of brightwork.
  • Clean toilet seats on both sides.
  • Scour and sanitise all washbasins.
  • Remove splash marks from walls around washbasins.
  • Report any restroom repairs or maintenance requirements to the SNV Operations Department.
  • Clean and wipe restroom partitions on both sides.
  • Pour fresh water into floor drains as necessary to maintain the sewer line, with particular attention to Saturdays.
  • Provide and maintain a list of cleaning staff assigned to the SNV premises.
  • Provide designated staff to support tea and coffee service in the kitchen, as required and agreed with SNV.

3.2 Cleaning equipment and materials 

The selected service provider shall supply all cleaning equipment, cleaning chemicals, waste bags, paper towels, hand soap, toilet paper required to perform the services. The services are intended to cover approximately 934 square metres of office space and up to fifty (50) staff members at the SNV Country Office. Restocking requirements shall be coordinated with the SNV Operations Office.

3.3 Reporting Damage

The selected service provider shall promptly report any damaged facilities, fixtures or broken items to the SNV Operations Officer. Such reports should be made at least bi-weekly and immediately where the damage requires urgent attention, to ensure that the service provider is not held responsible for pre-existing or reported damage.

4. Quotation and price requirement 

Quotations shall be submitted in Rwandan Francs (RWF) and shall be presented as fixed prices. The quotation shall remain valid for at least forty-five (45) calendar days from the submission deadline.

Quoted prices shall remain fixed for the initial twelve (12)-month contract period, unless a price adjustment is mutually agreed by the parties and justified by significant changes in market conditions.

Offerors shall submit their quotation using their official quotation format or company letterhead and shall provide a clear breakdown of the proposed costs in the required price schedule.

5. Taxes and statutory requirements

All quoted prices shall be inclusive of all applicable taxes, charges, tariffs, duties and levies.

Offerors shall provide the following supporting documents, as applicable:

  • A signed cover letter containing the full contact details of the person authorised to receive correspondence, including name, position, email address and telephone number.
  • VAT registration certificate, where applicable.
  • Valid Rwanda Development Board (RDB) registration certificate, where applicable.
  • Valid Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) tax clearance certificate.
  • Valid business registration certificate or business licence, including evidence of compliance with applicable social security requirements.

6. Eligibility: By submitting an offer in response to this RFQ, the offeror certifies that the company and its principal officers are not debarred, suspended or otherwise considered ineligible to participate in procurement under applicable Rwandan laws or relevant international requirements. SNV will not award a contract to any firm that is debarred, suspended or otherwise ineligible.

7. Evaluation and Award: 

The award will be made to a responsible and eligible offeror whose quotation complies with the RFQ requirements and provides the best value to SNV based on the evaluation criteria below.

Evaluation Criterion Description Maximum Score
Technical responsiveness / compliance Extent to which the bidder meets the required cleaning specifications and demonstrates adequate capacity, including personnel, equipment, cleaning materials, and proposed approach to delivering the services. 25
Company experience and track record Demonstrated experience (minimum three years) in providing office cleaning or similar services, supported by evidence of previous or current comparable assignments (At least three Certificates) and client references. 35
Financial proposal / price Overall cost of the proposed services, supported by a clear and complete price breakdown. 40

Note: Offers with significant deficiencies in meeting the requirements may be considered non-responsive and disqualified. SNV reserves the right to waive immaterial deficiencies at its discretion.

8. Offer submission Checklist

To facilitate the preparation and review of offers, each offer should include the following:

  • Official quotation on company letterhead.
  • Signed statement confirming acceptance of the requirements and terms of this RFQ.
  • Completed price schedule with a clear cost breakdown.
  • Valid business registration certificate or business licence.
  • VAT certificate, where applicable.
  • Valid tax clearance certificate.
  • Evidence of relevant experience, including copies or references for similar contracts where available.
  • Complete contact details of the authorised contact person.

9. Submission of offers.

Completed quotations, together with all required supporting documentation, shall be submitted by email to rwandaprocurement@snv.org no later than 15 October 2026. The email subject line shall clearly state “Provision of Cleaning Services.”

Office Visit: Interested bidders may visit the office between 22nd to 30th September 2026, from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM, during which time access to the premises will be permitted.

10. Key compliance issues 

Consultant must comply with SNV’s environmental and Social Safeguarding policies and procedures as well as take into consideration donor-specific requirements. 

11. Data Protection assurance 

SNV will not retain your Personal Data for longer than is allowed by law or is necessary for the Purposes.

If you are selected and offered consultancy assignment, the Personal Data you have provided will be used by SNV for the purpose of this bidding administration. If you are unsuccessful on this occasion to secure tender with SNV, SNV will retain your Personal Data for required period for the purpose of any future internal or external audit.

Currency

1. About SNV and Background of the assignment

SNV SNV Netherlands Development Organization is a not-for-profit international development organization founded in the Netherlands in 1965 with a global presence in 30 countries across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. As an organization, SNV focuses on the Agriculture, WASH, and Energy sectors with the belief that no one should have to live in poverty and that all people should have the opportunity to pursue their own sustainable development. SNV contributes to these sectors by strengthening the capacity of targeted partners and communities at the field level to realize increased skill sets and sustainable performance; reduce poverty levels and expand employment; and improve food security while paying special attention to gender equity, social inclusion of marginalized groups and stakeholder accountability.

1.2. Background of the Assignment

SNV Rwanda invites reputable and experienced companies to submit quotations for the provision of Kitchen Supplies and refreshments. The selected service provider will provide Kitchen supplies and refreshments as it is listed below on an as-needed basis for a period of twelve (12) months, in accordance with the requirements and terms set out in this RFQ.

Offerors are responsible for ensuring that their quotations are submitted in accordance with the instructions, requirements, terms and conditions contained in this RFQ. Failure to comply with the requirements may result in the offer being considered non-responsive.

2. General Instructions and conditions

This is a Request for Quotations only. Issuance of this RFQ does not obligate SNV to make an award or reimburse any costs incurred by an offeror in preparing or submitting an offer.

1. Any award resulting from this RFQ will be formalised through an appropriate SNV contractual instrument.

2. SNV reserves the right to request clarifications or negotiate with any offeror before making an award.

3. SNV may make a partial award or split the award among more than one service provider where this is considered to be in SNV's best interest.

4. SNV reserves the right to cancel the RFQ at any time.

5. Payment will normally be made within thirty (30) calendar days after receipt of a valid invoice and confirmation that the services have been satisfactorily delivered and accepted.

6. Release of payment is subject to satisfactory performance and written acceptance of the services in accordance with the RFQ and the resulting contract or purchase order.

Terms of reference and Service requirements

SNV is seeking offers from reputable, well established and experienced offerors, duly incorporated under the Laws of Rwanda to provide Kitchen Supplies under a Fixed Contract Agreement (FCA), at fixed prices for a period of 12 months.

3. Responsibilities of offeror (Company, supplier or vendor)

4. Quotation and price requirement

Quotations shall be submitted in Rwandan Francs (RWF) and shall be presented as fixed prices. The quotation shall remain valid for at least forty-five (45) calendar days from the submission deadline.

Quoted prices shall remain fixed for the initial twelve (12)-month contract period, unless a price adjustment is mutually agreed by the parties and justified by significant changes in market conditions.

Offerors shall submit their quotation using their official quotation format or company letterhead and shall provide a clear breakdown of the proposed costs in the required price schedule.

5. Taxes and statutory requirements

All quoted prices shall be inclusive of all applicable taxes, charges, tariffs, duties and levies.

Offerors shall provide the following supporting documents, as applicable:

  • Valid business registration certificate or business licence, including evidence of compliance with applicable social security requirements.
  • Valid Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) tax clearance certificate.
  • Valid Rwanda Development Board (RDB) registration certificate, where applicable.
  • VAT registration certificate, where applicable.
  • A signed cover letter containing the full contact details of the person authorised to receive correspondence, including name, position, email address and telephone number.

6. Eligibility: By submitting an offer in response to this RFQ, the offeror certifies that the company and its principal officers are not debarred, suspended or otherwise considered ineligible to participate in procurement under applicable Rwandan laws or relevant international requirements. SNV will not award a contract to any firm that is debarred, suspended or otherwise ineligible.

7. Evaluation and Award:

The award will be made to a responsible and eligible offeror whose quotation complies with the RFQ requirements and provides the best value to SNV based on the evaluation criteria below.

Evaluation Criterion Description Maximum Score
Technical responsiveness / compliance Compliance with the required list of kitchen materials and refreshments, including the required specifications, quantities, quality requirements, packaging, and delivery requirements. The offeror must demonstrate its ability to supply all required items. 20
Company experience and track record Relevant experience in supplying kitchen materials, catering supplies, refreshments, beverages, snacks, or similar goods. Offerors should provide evidence of at least three (3) completion certificates from current or previous clients. 40
Financial proposal / prices Overall cost of the proposed supplies including unit prices, quantities, and all applicable taxes. 40

Note: Offers with significant deficiencies in meeting the requirements may be considered non-responsive and disqualified. SNV reserves the right to waive immaterial deficiencies at its discretion.

8. Offer submission Checklist

To facilitate the preparation and review of offers, each offer should include the following:

  • Official quotation on company letterhead.
  • Completed price schedule with a clear cost breakdown.
  • RDB Valid business registration certificate
  • Valid tax clearance certificate.
  • Evidence of relevant experience, including copies or references for similar contracts where available.
  • Complete contact details of the authorised contact person.

9. Submission of offers.

Completed quotations, together with all required supporting documentation, shall be submitted by email to rwandaprocurement@snv.org no later than October 15, 2026. The email subject line shall clearly state “Supply of Kitchen Materials and Refreshments.”

Key compliance issues

Consultant must comply with SNV’s environmental and Social Safeguarding policies and procedures as well as take into consideration donor-specific requirements.

Data Protection assurance

SNV will not retain your Personal Data for longer than is allowed by law or is necessary for the Purposes.

If you are selected and offered consultancy assignment, the Personal Data you have provided will be used by SNV for the purpose of this bidding administration. If you are unsuccessful on this occasion to secure tender with SNV, SNV will retain your Personal Data for required period for the purpose of any future internal or external audit.

greatrwandajobs.title: Provision of Operation and Maintenance Services of Oxygen PSA Plants in Rwanda Hospitals tender at Rwanda Medical Supply Limited
greatrwandajobs.description:
Provision of Operation and Maintenance Services of Oxygen PSA Plants in Rwanda Hospitals Tender at Rwanda Medical Supply Ltd

Medical oxygen is an essential medicine for which there are no alternatives. It is required to treat chronic and acute conditions and to conduct safe surgeries and oxygen is included on the World Health Organization (WHO) list of Essential Medicines. In Rwanda, it is designated by the Ministry of Health (MOH) of Rwanda as an essential inhalation medicine.

The public supply of medical oxygen should be sustained and reach all those in need. Due to Government of Rwanda (GOR) investments, 28 of 55 public health facilities currently have one or more oxygen production plants on site. Overall, these plants combined have a maximum oxygen production capacity of 20,300,000 L per day or approximately 406,000 cylinders (50L) per month.

Recent investments by the GOR and its partners have increased the oxygen production capacity of public hospitals and most of public health facilities are equipped with medical gas piping systems for easy and safe delivery of medical oxygen to the bedside. Although a remarkable progress, there are still some barriers to be addressed; in the production, and distribution including the PSA plants maintenance.

The GoR, through the Ministry of Health (MoH), Rwanda Biomedical Centre (RBC), Clinton Heath Access Initiative (CHAI) and Rwanda Medical Supply (RMS), intends to establish a Partnership under an Operate–Maintain–Replace (OMR) model to ensure sustainable, equitable, and reliable access to medical oxygen across public health facilities in Rwanda.

The partnership will leverage the existing national network of PSA oxygen plants distributed across public hospitals and associated health facilities. The selected contractor(s) shall assume responsibility for operation, maintenance, distribution, lifecycle management, and replacement of designated oxygen production assets while ownership of the assets remains with the GOR. This TOR provides a framework to guide the contractor(s) in the respective scopes of work to ensure continued and reliable access to oxygen.

The Competitive Dialogue process is being undertaken with selected supplier(s) to refine the final technical, operational, commercial, legal, and contractual structure before issuing the final tender and contract award..

2. Objective of the Competitive Dialogue

The objective of the Competitive Dialogue is to engage oxygen PSA plants’ suppliers in structured discussions to refine and optimize the proposed model and support the development of a bankable, sustainable, and performance-based procurement structure.

Specifically, the dialogue aims to:

  • Validate the operational feasibility of the OMR model;
  • Determine optimal lot configuration and hub allocation arrangements;
  • Define efficient oxygen production and distribution models;
  • Establish sustainable operation, maintenance and asset replacement mechanisms;
  • Define measurable service levels and key performance indicators (KPIs);
  • Establish surge preparedness and emergency response mechanisms;
  • Ensure affordability, value for money, and long-term sustainability;
  • Finalize the contractual and payment framework.

3. SCOPE OF PROCUREMENT

3.1 Operation of PSA Oxygen Plants

The operator shall:

  • Operate designated PSA oxygen plants and associated infrastructure;
  • Optimize PSA plants placement across the network
  • Ensure continuous oxygen production in accordance with required purity and quality standards.;
  • Manage plant staffing, operational scheduling, utilities coordination, and production planning;
  • Plan the demand and supply of medical oxygen its designated areas
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable health, environmental, and safety regulations.
  • Operator shall have the minimum national oxygen reserve stock and filled backup cylinders

3.2 Maintenance and Asset Management

The operator shall:

  • Conduct preventive, corrective, and emergency maintenance for all assigned equipment;
  • Maintain PSA plants in accordance with manufacturer standards and specifications;
  • Ensure availability of spare parts and consumables;
  • Develop and implement lifecycle management plans for all assigned assets;
  • Replace end-of-life equipment and major components in accordance with agreed contractual requirements;
  • Maintain accurate maintenance logs and asset registers.
  • The operator shall return all government-owned assets in good operating condition, subject to independent technical verification

3.3 Oxygen Distribution Services

The operator shall:

  • Manage end-to-end oxygen distribution through the designated hub-and-spoke network;
  • Invest in cylinders, filling equipment, and distribution fleet (All sizes of oxygen cylinders, trucks, trolleys,)
  • Ensure timely refill and delivery of oxygen cylinders to all assigned health facilities up to primary health level facilities including ambulances.
  • Optimize transport routes and delivery schedules;
  • Maintain adequate cylinder tracking and inventory management systems;
  • Ensure uninterrupted supply within the agreed service coverage area.

3.4 Quality Assurance and Regulatory Compliance

The operator shall:

  • Ensure oxygen purity meets applicable medical standards;
  • Maintain calibration and testing systems for quality verification for both PSAs and cylinders;
  • Comply with Rwanda FDA, MoH, RBC, and other applicable regulatory requirements;
  • Establish quality assurance protocols and incident reporting mechanisms.

3.5 Risk Mitigation for Emergency Preparedness 

  • The contingency framework will include two levels of reserve oxygen stock. First, each PSA plant operator shall maintain a minimum reserve equivalent to 100 cylinders of oxygen at each lot.
  • By design, the contractor will maintain a reasonable number of competing PSA plant operators to promote supply security, operational resilience, and market stability. No merger or monopoly arrangement shall be permitted under this framework, and no single oxygen PSA operator shall supply more than 35% of the national public-sector medical oxygen demand. 
  • The contractor will also require mandatory performance bond arrangements throughout the contractual period. This mechanism will protect both the GOR and the PSA plant operators while promoting sustainable and reliable medical oxygen supply through a partnership model based on mutual accountability and shared benefits. 
  • Operators shall maintain adequate stocks of preventive and corrective maintenance spare parts, as well as emergency cylinder filling and backup supply mechanisms. Considering the lifespan and replacement schedules of critical equipment and components, operators will be required to plan and execute maintenance and replacement activities proactively to avoid any interruption in medical oxygen supply. 
  • While optimization is a primary objective, any relocation, consolidation, or repurposing of PSA plants shall be carefully assessed and justified based on the availability of adequate and reliable alternative sources of medical oxygen supply. No movement of PSA infrastructure shall occur without comprehensive contingency planning, formal risk assessment, and mutual agreement with the designated representative of the GoR. 

3.6 Financing

  • Cover all needed CAPEX to run the network including but not cylinders, distribution trucks, relocating PSAs, replacing PSA, supply chain management tools
  • Cover all operational costs needed to operate the production including but not limited to staffing, maintenance and repair of equipment, power supply, and other utilities, administrative and office costs.
  • Revenue will be recovered from supplying oxygen to health facilities per cubic meter
  • Oxygen will be delivered on standardized tariff per cubic meter delivered to health facility

4. Key Discussion Areas During Competitive Dialogue

The Competitive Dialogue process will focus on the following areas:

4.1 Technical and Operational Structure

  • Hub allocation and lot structure;
  • Management of co-located PSA facilities;
  • Production optimization strategies;
  • Fleet and cylinder management systems;
  • Transition arrangements from current operational structures.

4.2 Commercial and Financial Structure

  • Payment mechanisms;
  • Output-based financing arrangements;
  • Tariff structure and affordability considerations;
  • Asset replacement financing mechanisms;
  • Revenue sustainability and commercial viability.

4.3 Contractual and Risk Allocation

  • Allocation of operational, maintenance, and demand risks;
  • Force majeure and emergency response obligations;
  • Performance guarantees and penalties;
  • Contract duration and renewal provisions.

4.4 Performance Management

The dialogue shall define KPIs including but not limited to:

  • Plant uptime;
  • Asset condition score
  • Oxygen purity compliance;
  • Delivery lead times;
  • Order fulfillment rates;
  • Stock out days per facility
  • Cylinder turnaround time
  • Reporting compliance
  • Safety incident rate
  • Maintenance response times; Emergency response readiness
  • Strategic stock level (days of cover)
  • Spare part stock availability

5. Deliverables Expected from Bidders

Shortlisted bidders participating in the dialogue process shall be expected to provide:

  • Initial technical and operational proposals;
  • Proposed lot allocation and hub management approach;
  • Proposed maintenance and lifecycle management strategy;
  • Proposed distribution and logistics model;
  • Proposed staffing and technical support arrangements;
  • Preliminary commercial and financial model to the different cost centers;
  • Risk allocation recommendations;
  • Proposed service level agreements and KPIs;
  • Emergency preparedness and business continuity plans;
  • Recommendations for contract structure and implementation arrangements.

6. Eligibility requirements

Interested bidders are required to submit the following documents:

  1. A letter addressed to Rwanda Medical Supply expressing the interest in participating in the oxygen PSA plant O&M PPP model
  2. A signed technical proposal of PSA plant operation and maintenance approach
  3. Valid company certificate of incorporation/Business registration certificate
  4. Valid tax clearance certificate
  5. At least 3 years experience in the operation and maintenance of PSA plants, proven by 2 good completion certificates or contracts, with a combined cost not less than 500,000,000 Frw
  6. Requirements for Engineers: 2
  • Bachelor’s degree in any of the following fields: Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Biomedical Engineering proven by a copy of the degree certificate
  • At least 2 years’ experience in operation and maintenance of PSA plants
  • Update curriculum vitae
  1. Requirements for technicians: 4
  • Diploma in any of the following fields: Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Biomedical Engineering proven by a copy of the degree certificate
  • At least 1 years experience in operation and maintenance of PSA plants
  • Update curriculum vitae
  1. Local bidders are required to provide any PSA plant manufacturer authorization

7. Duration of the Contract

The anticipated contract duration shall be discussed during the Competitive Dialogue process and may include provisions for renewal based on performance and achievement of contractual obligations.

8. PPP Framework

  • The framework will be overseen by a MOH designated multidisciplinary Performance Review Technical Working Group (TWG). The TWG will support the RMS designated Contract Manager in managing overall contract(s) performance, evaluating key performance indicators (KPIs), reviewing compliance with contractual obligations, including maintenance and asset replacement requirements, and providing technical recommendations on contractual decisions and corrective actions where necessary.
  • The TWG will comprise representatives from the MOH, Rwanda Biomedical Centre (RBC), RMS, the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), and other development partners supporting the GOR in strengthening the national medical oxygen ecosystem. The TWG will support the proper transition, operational oversight, and asset management of the oxygen PSA plants throughout the PPP lifecycle.
  • In collaboration with the host institutions and relevant government entities, the TWG will also follow up on the continuity of supply arrangements and ensure sustained access to essential utilities and infrastructure required for uninterrupted PSA plant operations, including electricity, water, and network connectivity. The TWG will serve as the technical coordination and oversight arm for the effective implementation of the PPP framework, from transition and operationalization through final contractual completion.
  • Working closely with the designated Contract Manager, the TWG will support the establishment and effective implementation of standardized systems for oxygen measurement across production, storage, and distribution operations, as well as quality assurance, monitoring, reporting, and real-time operational oversight. The TWG will also promote and support data-driven performance management, transparency, accountability, and continuous quality improvement to ensure a sustainable, efficient, resilient, and uninterrupted national medical oxygen supply system.

9. Governing Framework

The Competitive Dialogue and subsequent procurement process shall be conducted in accordance with:

  • Rwanda Medical supply procurement policy;
  • Rwanda Medical Supply PPP regulatory framework;
  • Applicable health sector regulations and policies;
  • Any additional guidance issued by the Government of Rwanda.

10. PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE


The competitive dialogue procedure will follow these key steps:

Phase I.

  1. Call for Initial Proposals: Interested bidders are invited to submit the proposals in response to this tender. The documents required at this stage are specified in section VI
  2. Shortlisting of Bidders: Bidders will be shortlisted based on evaluation findings of initial proposals as described in section VI.

Phase II:

  1. Dialogue Phase
    RMS will conduct structured dialogues with each of the shortlisted bidders. During this phase:
    • Technical specifications will be refined.
    • Confidentiality will be maintained for all bidder-specific information unless explicitly agreed otherwise.
    • Equal treatment of all bidders will be ensured.
  2. Submission of Final Offers
    After the dialogue phase concludes and specifications are finalized, RMS will invite final offers from all shortlisted suppliers.
  3. Evaluation and Contract Award

Final offers will be evaluated based on the established evaluation criteria. The contract will be awarded to the most economically and technically advantageous offer.

11. SUBMISSION GUIDELINES

Interested suppliers are invited to submit initial proposals by 30/9/2026 at 10:00am local time

Submissions must be made only electronically to our confidential email: tenders@rms.rw with the subject line: “Tender for oxygen PSA plant Operation”.

For questions and clarifications, please contact rms.procurement@rms.rw with a copy to cgatsinzi@rms.rw ,jmvnkurunziza@rms.rw, jczimurida@rms.rw and erugamba@rms.rw

greatrwandajobs.description:
Expression of interest for qualified local Rwandan service providers to undertake Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) monitoring services Tender at Trinity Musha Mines Limited

Trinity Metals (Trinity Nyakabingo mines ,Trinity Rutongo mines and Trinity Musha mines Limited) invites Expressions of Interest from qualified experts and service providers to undertake independent Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) monitoring across its mining operations. The assignment is intended to establish a historical deformation baseline and provide continuous, independent quarterly monitoring of waste rock facilities, tailings storage facilities, and ground subsidence to achieve precise stability data.

1. Scope of Work

The scope of the InSAR monitoring services includes, but is not limited to, the following:

  • Establish a historical displacement baseline utilizing a minimum of 2 years of archived SAR satellite imagery.
  • Provide continuous surface displacement monitoring, delivering update reports to provide independent technical assurance.
  • Monitor ground displacements across critical infrastructure, specifically focusing on waste dumps, tailings storage facilities, and areas impacted by underground mining or subsidence.
  • Measure displacements of the ground's surface at the millimetre scale. 
  • Calculate and model the line-of-sight (LOS), vertical, and east-west components of the surface displacement.
  • Distil the geotechnically relevant signal from the geotechnically irrelevant noise.
  • Provide comprehensive reports that highlight displacement anomalies where velocity rates have accelerated compared to the historical baseline.

2. Eligibility and Competency Requirements

Interested parties must:

  • Have demonstrated expertise in interferometry and geodetic estimation techniques.
  • Preferably possess proprietary software, algorithms, and intellectual data processing capabilities for InSAR data processing. 
  • Demonstrate the ability to utilize advanced processing techniques, such as Persistent Scatterer Interferometry (PSI) combining persistent and distributed scatterers, or Small Baseline Subset (SBAS) approaches.
  • Possess the capability to account for, process, and visualize SAR geometric effects inherent in steep mining terrain, including radar shadow, foreshortening, and layover.
  • Have a proven track record of providing satellite InSAR monitoring services across the mining industry.

All interested service providers should submit an Expression of Interest together with the following supporting documents:

  • Cover letter introducing the company or individual consultant, confirming interest, availability, and understanding of the technical assignment.
  • Company profile detailing InSAR technical capabilities, proprietary processing tools, and domain expertise.
  • Summary of similar InSAR surface displacement monitoring assignments undertaken for the mining industry.
  • Proposed methodology for establishing the 2-year historical baseline and conducting the ongoing quarterly analysis.
  • CVs of proposed personnel clearly demonstrating experience in undertaking of InSAR monitoring work. 
  • Summary of at least three similar assignments undertaken in the last five years, including client name, project scope, location, and contactable references. 
  • Certificate of domestic company registration issued by RDB.
  • VAT registration certificate, where applicable.
  • Valid tax clearance certificate issued by RRA.

Submissions should be forwarded to tender@trinity-metals.com  no later than 30 September 2026 at 11:00 AM local time.

Expressions of Interest received after 11:00 AM local time on 30 September 2026 will not be considered.

Shortlisted respondents may be invited for further technical discussions to confirm capability and suitability. Thereafter, Trinity Metals may issue an invitation to tender to selected qualified bidders.

Trinity Metals (Trinity Nyakabingo mines ,Trinity Rutongo mines and Trinity Musha mines Limited) invites Expressions of Interest from qualified software service providers to supply a comprehensive geotechnical engineering software suite across its mining operations. Scope of Work

The scope of the software provision and technical support includes, but is not limited to, the

following:

  • Provision of multi-seat annual lease licenses for 3D finite element analysis (FEA) software or integrated suite capable of:
    • Evaluating soil and rock mechanics, 3D excavation design, tunnelling, support design, and groundwater seepage.
    • 3D stability analysis software for evaluating underground excavations in jointed rock and modelling intersecting rock wedges.
    • Graphical and statistical analysis tools for orientation-based geological data, stereonet plotting, and kinematic analysis of rock slopes.

  • Be an established developer or authorized provider of globally recognized geotechnical engineering software, with demonstrated application in hard rock underground mining environments.

  • Ensure the software suite is fully compatible with standard corporate IT environments, specifically Windows 64-bit systems.
  • Demonstrate compliance with data protection and privacy laws (such as Rwanda Law No. 058/2021 or equivalent international standards), including appropriate technical and organisational measures for data security.

  • Have a minimum of 10 years demonstrated rock/geotechnical engineering experience in hard rock underground mining, including work on mine infrastructure stability such as road slopes, and waste rock facilities.
  • Possess a solid track record of working on external consultancy assignments, technical rock engineering audits, numerical modelling, geotechnical peer reviews, or independent geotechnical assurance reviews.

greatrwandajobs.title: Front Office Officer job at SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
greatrwandajobs.description:
Context of the position:

SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Front Office Officer, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.

JOB PURPOSE

The main role for this position is to provide professional, efficient, and welcoming front-office and administrative support by managing the reception area, receiving and directing visitors and calls, handling correspondence, and providing timely assistance to staff and external stakeholders. The Front Office Officer ensures effective communication and smooth day-to-day front-office operations while maintaining a professional image of the organization and safeguarding confidential information.

Main clients:

  • All SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda staff and departments
  • All visitors, guests, and members of the public coming to SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
  • Children, young people, families, and other programme participants visiting the organization
  • Government institutions, partners, donors, service providers, and other external stakeholders
  • Candidates, consultants, and other individuals visiting SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda for official purposes

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:

The Front Office Officer is responsible for managing the reception area and serving as the first point of contact for visitors, staff, partners, and other stakeholders. The position ensures professional handling of telephone calls, correspondence, visitors, and general inquiries while providing timely administrative support. The officer maintains accurate front-office records, ensures compliance with safeguarding, confidentiality, and security procedures, and contributes to creating a welcoming and professional image of SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda. Below are the details:

Reception and Customer Service

  • Receive and welcome all visitors, guests, and stakeholders in a professional and courteous manner.
  • Identify visitors and direct them to the appropriate staff members or departments.
  • Ensure that visitors receive timely and accurate information and assistance.
  • Maintain a professional, clean, and welcoming reception environment.
  • Handle inquiries and provide appropriate responses or referrals.

Telephone and Communication Management

  • Receive and manage incoming telephone calls and direct them to the appropriate staff members.
  • Take and relay messages accurately and promptly.
  • Manage general front-office email inquiries and ensure that correspondence is directed to the relevant departments.
  • Support effective communication between staff, visitors, and external stakeholders.

Visitor and Front Office Administration

  • Maintain accurate records of visitors, appointments, deliveries, and other front-office activities.
  • Manage visitor access in accordance with organizational security and safeguarding procedures.
  • Coordinate appointments and meeting arrangements as required.
  • Receive and distribute incoming correspondence, documents, and deliveries.
  • Maintain an organized filing system for front-office records.

Administrative Support

  • Provide general administrative support to the Administration and other departments as assigned.
  • Support the preparation and coordination of meetings, events, and official visits.
  • Assist with photocopying, scanning, printing, document distribution, and other routine administrative tasks.
  • Support the coordination of office supplies and other front-office requirements.

Safeguarding, Confidentiality and Security

  • Ensure that all visitors and stakeholders are treated in accordance with SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda's safeguarding standards and procedures.
  • Maintain confidentiality of organizational, staff, visitor, and programme-related information.
  • Immediately report any safeguarding, security, or other concerns through the appropriate channels.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies, procedures, and health and safety requirements.

Professional Representation

  • Serve as the first point of contact for SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda and promote a professional and positive image of the organization.
  • Maintain professional conduct and demonstrate respect, integrity, and courtesy in all interactions.
  • Build positive working relationships with staff, visitors, partners, government representatives, and other stakeholders.

Reporting and Other Responsibilities

  • Prepare routine front-office reports and maintain relevant records as required.
  • Monitor and report issues affecting the smooth operation of the reception area.
  • Perform any other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the supervisor.

Child Protection Policy

  • At all times, avoid actions or behaviour that could be construed as poor or potentially abusive practice.
  • Report any child safeguarding concerns immediately in accordance with the organizational’s Child Protection Policy
  • Promote and uphold the organisation’s values and child safeguarding principles in all interactions and decision – making

Data Protection Policy.

  • At all times ensure that personal data of SOS Children’s Villages beneficiaries and their families as well as SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda co-workers is handled confidentially and in accordance with prevailing SOS Children’s Villages.
  • Ensure that personal sponsor information and data used and administered for the benefit of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda, is stored and transferred securely, handled confidentially and in accordance with prevailing data protection laws. Donor data will remain under the control of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda and shall not be forwarded to or swapped with other organizations.

Required key skills set.

Must have the following:

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Strong customer service and reception skills
  • Good organizational and time-management skills
  • Professional, courteous, and welcoming attitude
  • Good telephone and email communication skills
  • Attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information
  • Good computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications
  • Ability to work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds
  • Problem-solving skills and ability to work under pressure

Formal qualifications

Education: Diploma in Front Office Management, Business Admin, or related field

Professional Qualification: Customer Service certification preferred

Experience requirements

Experience: 3+ years reception/front office experience; corporate environment

Skills & Competencies: Reception Management, Telephone Etiquette, Visitor Management, Mail Handling, Office Administration, Professional Presentation, Customer Service Orientation, English & Kinyarwanda fluency.

greatrwandajobs.title: Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation job at SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
greatrwandajobs.description:
Context of the position:

SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.

JOB PURPOSE

To move ICT from 'fixing laptops' to 'leveraging technology' for social impact. The Senior Manager, ICT and Programmes Digitalisation leads SOS Rwanda's ICT function and drives the organisation's digital transformation agenda, designing and implementing ICT strategy, managing all ICT systems and infrastructure, leading the digitalisation of programme and operational workflows, implementing secure digital case management platforms, ensuring cybersecurity and data protection, and building staff digital literacy across all four Program Areas.

The position is the functional supervisor of the ICT Administrator in Kigali and provides technical oversight to location-level ICT focal points.

Main clients:

  • Deputy National Director for Operations
  • National Director
  • All National Management Team (NMT) members
  • Head of Finance — ERP and financial systems
  • Head of MEAL — digital MEL platforms
  • Head of HROD — HRIS systems
  • Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics — procurement systems
  • Programme teams across all four area offices
  • SOS Regional ICT Advisor (ESAF) and SOS International ICT teams
  • ICT Administrator- Kigali (direct report)

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:

ICT Strategy and Governance

  • Develop, implement, and update SOS Rwanda's ICT strategy — aligned with SOS Strategy 2030, MA Strategic Plan 2023–2027, and global SOS ICT standards.
  • Define national ICT budgets, procurement plans, and multi-year ICT investment roadmaps.
  • Develop and implement ICT policies and standards — covering architecture, security, disaster recovery, procurement, and service provision.
  • Participate in regional ICT knowledge-sharing processes and coordinate with the SOS ESAF ICT Advisor on global standards and initiatives.
  • Lead ICT governance — including vendor management, service level agreements, and ICT committee oversight.

Programmes Digitalisation & Digital Case Management

  • Implement and manage a secure, cloud-based digital case management platform for tracking child progress — ensuring data privacy and compliance with Rwanda data protection laws and SOS-KDI data protection rules.
  • Lead the digitalisation of SOS Rwanda's programme functions — introducing digital case management, beneficiary tracking, and electronic documentation workflows across all four locations.
  • Equip field staff with mobile tools for real-time community reporting — reducing the 'paperwork lag' and improving data quality.
  • Drive paperless operations across all locations — designing change management plans that support staff adoption of new digital tools.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Strategy and Programme Implementation and the MEAL function to align digitalisation initiatives with programme quality and RBM needs.
  • Explore, evaluate, and pilot AI adoption and knowledge management tools that enhance programme decision-making and organisational efficiency.

ERP, HRIS and Operational Systems

  • Oversee the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of SOS Rwanda's ERP system — ensuring integration across finance, procurement, HR, and programme functions.
  • Manage the HRIS system — ensuring data integrity, user access management, and alignment with HR processes.
  • Lead the digitisation of procurement and supply chain systems in coordination with the Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics.
  • Ensure all ICT systems are properly integrated, reducing data silos and enabling organisation-wide reporting and analytics.

Infrastructure, Cybersecurity and Business Continuity

  • Manage SOS Rwanda's IT network and server infrastructure across all locations — ensuring 99%+ system uptime, reliability, performance, and cost-effectiveness.
  • Develop and implement a comprehensive cybersecurity framework — including data protection, access control, threat monitoring, and incident response — ensuring the cybersecurity audit score meets SOS-KDI standards.
  • Ensure compliance with SOS-KDI data protection rules and Rwanda data protection regulations, including the privacy of child and family records.
  • Design and maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans — ensuring operational resilience in the event of system failures.

Digital Literacy & Capacity Building

  • Build digital literacy across SOS Rwanda — designing and delivering ICT training programmes for staff at all levels and locations.
  • Supervise the ICT Administrator and provide technical oversight to location ICT focal points.
  • Coach programme and operations staff on effective use of digital tools for monitoring, reporting, and case management.
  • Train community partners and staff on using technology for education, health monitoring, and economic strengthening.

Formal qualifications and Experiencerequirements:

Education & Professional Qualifications

  • Master’s or bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or related field (Master's preferred for Grade 5).
  • ITIL, PMP, or relevant technical certifications required (Grade 5 requirement).
  • Cybersecurity certification (CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or equivalent) is a strong advantage.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum of 7 years of progressive ICT experience; 3+ years in senior ICT leadership or digital transformation role.
  • Demonstrated experience leading digital transformation initiatives in an INGO, NGO, or complex multi-site organisation.
  • Proven experience with ERP systems (SOS ERP, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, or equivalent) and HRIS platforms.
  • Strong track record in cybersecurity management, data protection, and ICT governance.
  • Experience with ICT4D tools — digital case management, mobile data collection, cloud platforms.
  • Experience working across multiple sites and geographically dispersed teams.

Skills & Competencies

  • Digital Transformation Strategy and Programme Digitisation.
  • ICT Infrastructure Management and Systems Architecture.
  • Data Governance and Cybersecurity.
  • ERP Systems Management and Integration.
  • Vendor Management and contract administration.
  • Strong change management and adult learning facilitation skills.
  • Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
  • Good understanding of programme monitoring, MEAL, and data analytics.
  • Fluent English; Kinyarwanda and/or French is an advantage.
  • Commitment to SOS values and ethical use of data and technology in child-related programmes.

greatrwandajobs.title: Institutional Partnership Development Specialist job at SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
greatrwandajobs.description:
Context of the position:

SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Institutional Partnership Development Specialist, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.

JOB PURPOSE

The Institutional Partnership Development Specialist mobilizes institutional funding for SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda and is a key contributor to the growth of the IPD funding portfolio and day to day donor relationship management with bilateral donors, international donors, embassies, diplomatic missions, foundations to significantly increase the financial resources for national programs. This role involves developing and implementing institutional partnership plans, developing funding proposals to expand the organization’s programs and contributing to donor compliance.

Main clients:

Internal – National Director, Deputy National Director – Operations, Director of Program Quality, Safeguarding and Partnership Development, Head of Fund Development and Partnerships, Program Managers, Project teams, finance team, and PSA staff

External – Institutional Donors, Implementing partners, Government, NGOs, Embassies, Diplomatic Missions, Foundations

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:

Fundraising and Donor Liaison

  • Develop and implement annual IPD plans in line with the national organizational strategy annual set targets.
  • Ensure IPD annual targets are met according to the national organizational strategy.
  • Identify monthly IPD funding opportunities from in-country, bilateral, multilateral, international donors, embassies, diplomatic missions and foundations to meet annual targets.
  • Develop and write program ideas, concept notes, expression of interests, grant applications, technical project proposals for IPD projects while ensuring they are provisioned with available information prior to involving additional teams.
  • Conduct comprehensive background research on relevant policies, political, economic, environmental factors, and existing strategies at national, sub-national, regional, and global levels to contextualize project proposal descriptions.
  • Develop different project proposal sections, including risk factors, mitigation measures, sustainable development impacts, paradigm shifts, result frameworks, impact matrices, problem and objective trees, stakeholder analyses and others.
  • Ensure the timely collection of content needed from program teams for high quality and competitive proposal development.
  • Facilitate the development of project proposals and organize proposal development workshops with program team, partners and/or stakeholders, serving as the focal point for coordination and logistics.
  • Together with the Head of Fund Development and Partnership and program team identify suitable lead applications, co-applicants and implementing partners to increase competitiveness in bid applications.

Donor Compliance Monitoring

  • Regularly update the master partner landscape and partner mapping to reflect current information.
  • Update IPD project grant compliance matrices to ensure adherence to donor requirements.
  • Ensure that project one-pagers and program summaries are always current and accurate.
  • Maintain an up-to-date master list of IPD grants, including grant descriptions.
  • Facilitate project start following funding approvals.
  • Monitor changes in IPD projects, advise the Program Team on documenting amendments, and communicate risks effectively.
  • Monitor donor grant requirements to ensure compliance, providing advice on cost extensions, non-cost extensions, agreement addendums, and other contractual issues.
  • Monitor project spending to prevent overspending or underspending and advise project teams accordingly.
  • Oversee project implementation from compliance perspective, advising teams on contractual clauses, amendments, risk management, and supporting timely project delivery.
  • Support Donor Monitoring Field visits: Coordinate with relevant team members and stakeholders, prepare one pager, arrange logistics, accompany monitoring field visits.
  • Track donor monitoring network meetings, maintain detailed minutes, and keep records of donor interactions and follow-ups.
  • Ensure proper documentation of all project amendments, and donor correspondence.
  • Train project team on donor grant compliance, funding policies, donor relations, donor reporting, contract management, etc
  • Prepare and submit IPD weekly, monthly updates and quarterly IPD reports

Donor Contract Management

  • Prepare, coordinate, and develop partner due diligence reports and maintain filing systems.
  • Develop and maintain a mechanism for management of IPD Partnership agreements and signature processes, including contract/partnership agreement preparation, and preparation of consortium agreements.
  • Ensure all funding files (electronic, system and paper) are complete, filed and kept up to date.
  • Register and update SOS Rwanda project proposal development information in ProDIGI software

Partnership Development and Networking

  • Establish and maintain regular contact with donors, attend donor forums, conferences etc
  • Identify and engage with in-country donors, foundation, embassies, diplomatic mission, bilateral, multilateral, international donors, to proactively explore and secure funding opportunities for IPD initiatives.
  • Develop partnerships and consortiums with other like-minded organizations and donors for purposes of bidding for large donor project proposals
  • Represent SOS Rwanda in sector level meetings (development and humanitarian/emergency) and other networking forums and use this to develop funding partnerships
  • Organize partnership roundtable meetings and networking meetings
  • Participate in regional IPD networking and training forums and contribute to development of new IPD strategies to improve practice

Formal qualifications and Experiencerequirements:

  • Excellent English language written skills are required for development of proposals
  • A holder of a bachelor’s degree in Sociology, Development studies, Economics or related field. Master’s degree will be an added advantage.
  • Excellent know how of project proposal writing skills is required, especially in the sectors of Child Protection, Alternative Care, Youth Empowerment, Livelihoods, Education, Health
  • He/she should have 5-8 years’ extensive experience in planning, securing and managing funds from institutional donors as well as a thorough understanding of writing of project proposal
  • Potential candidates should demonstrate evidence of medium/large proposals they have developed and won (0.5 – 2M USD)
  • A thorough understanding of Project Cycle Management is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Results-Based Management (RBM) approach is an additional asset
  • The post holder should have the following competencies flexibility, self-drive, attention to detail, respecting tight deadlines, ability to work with different teams in a fast-paced environment and ability to work independently.
  • He/she should be highly proficient in MS Word, Excel, Power-point and the use of Internet for research.

greatrwandajobs.description:
Position Summary

The Legal Advisor is the organization's dedicated in-house legal, risk and compliance authority, providing proactive legal counsel while owning enterprise risk management and the compliance program. The role is prospective and advisory in nature, embedded within management, and is deliberately distinct from the Internal Audit function, which independently and retrospectively tests whether policies and controls are being followed. The Legal Advisor reports directly to the General Manager and works closely with the Board on material legal, risk, and compliance matters.

Key Responsibilities

Legal Advisory

  • Draft, review, and negotiate contracts, including supplier agreements, OTA (online booking platform) contracts, event and banquet contracts, leases, franchise or management agreements, Sponsorship and Membership.
  • Maintain a central contract register and monitor important contractual deadlines and renewals.
  • Manage disputes, claims, and litigation in coordination with external counsel, protecting the organization's legal and financial position.
  • Provide legal opinions to the General Manager and Board on business decisions, new initiatives, and licensing matters.
  • Monitor and interpret changes in relevant law and regulation, including labor, licensing, consumer protection, and data privacy, and translate these into practical guidance for the business.
  • Manage corporate governance documentation, including board resolutions, the contracts registry, and intellectual property/trademark records.
  • Act as company representative in legal and regulatory matters, liaising with external counsel and regulators as required.

Risk Management

  • Build and maintain the enterprise risk register, covering operational, financial, reputational, and strategic risk.
  • Design and maintain the organization's risk appetite and risk treatment frameworks.
  • Lead crisis and incident response planning, including guest safety incidents, data breaches, and reputational or PR crises.
  • Own business continuity planning and periodic insurance adequacy reviews.

Compliance

  • Policy Development: write, update, and implement company policies, standards, and internal control systems, and lead their rollout across departments.
  • Design and own the organization's overall compliance program, including codes of conduct and supporting frameworks.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for regulators and licensing authorities (e.g., liquor licensing, tourism/hospitality regulation, fire and safety codes).
  • Monitor ongoing compliance with anti-money laundering (AML), data protection, labor, and health and safety regulations.
  • Conduct proactive compliance risk assessments and gap analyses, distinct from Internal Audit's control testing.
  • Staff Training: educate employees and leadership on compliance standards, codes of conduct, and new or changing legal requirements, through periodic training sessions.
  • Compliance Reviews & Reporting: run periodic internal compliance reviews, document findings, and report compliance issues and recommendations to the General Manager and, where material, the Board — distinct from Internal Audit's independent assurance testing.
  • Investigations: look into suspected policy violations or legal/regulatory breaches referred to the role and manage intake of the whistleblowing/ethics hotline (case management; investigations requiring independent audit assurance remain with Internal Audit).

Governance and Coordination

  • Maintain a clear delineation of duties from Internal Audit to avoid duplication and preserve Internal Audit's independence: the Legal Advisor builds and owns policies and frameworks; Internal Audit independently tests whether they are being followed.
  • Convene a quarterly coordination meeting with Internal Audit to align risk registers and avoid duplicated fieldwork.
  • Escalate material legal, risk, and compliance matters to the General Manager and, where warranted, directly to the Board.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in law (LLB), business, or a related field or relevant master's degree is an added advantage.
  • Must be a member in good standing with the Rwanda Bar Association (RBA), or demonstrate eligibility for admission (e.g., completion of a Diploma in Legal Practice from a recognized institution).
  • A postgraduate qualification or certification in Risk Management and/or Compliance (e.g., ICA Diploma in Compliance, CAMS for AML) is a strong advantage.
  • Minimum 5–8 years of post-qualification legal experience, ideally combining law firm and in-house exposure.
  • Demonstrated experience in contract negotiation and commercial law.
  • Prior exposure to regulatory liaison with licensing bodies, Labor authorities, and tax/AML regulators.
  • Hospitality, tourism, retail, or service-industry legal experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience building or running a compliance program from the ground up is a plus.

Key Competencies

  • Legal drafting and negotiation: contracts, policies, and memoranda of understanding.
  • Regulatory intelligence: ability to track and translate legal and regulatory change into business action.
  • Risk analysis: sound quantitative and qualitative risk assessment methodology.
  • Stakeholder management: able to advise the General Manager and Board while working cross-functionally with Operations, HR, and Finance.
  • Crisis management: composure and sound decision-making under incident pressure.
  • Communication: able to translate complex legal and regulatory language into practical guidance for non-legal staff (Front Office, F&B, Housekeeping, and other operational teams).
  • Integrity and independence of judgment: willing to escalate uncomfortable findings to management.
  • Attention to detail: precision in policy drafting, contract review, and compliance documentation.
  • Commercial pragmatism: advice that is workable for a fast-paced, guest-facing business rather than purely academic.

Scope Boundary with Internal Audit

To preserve Internal Audit's independence and avoid duplication of duties, the following remain explicitly outside the scope of this role:

  • Independent testing of control effectiveness (remains with Internal Audit).
  • Retrospective audit reporting to the Audit Committee/Board.
  • Assurance opinions on financial or operational controls.
  • Leading or opining on investigations requiring independent audit assurance (the Legal Advisor may support with legal input only).

  • Responsible for measuring metrics that support business goals, necessary aspects of human capital, and training and development.
  • Oversees the learning and development program in line with business requirements.
  • Ensures adherence to HC policies and procedures to promote a conducive working environment.
  • Responsible for promoting people wellness through the implementation of a wellness strategy.
  • Provides advice in disciplinary and grievance procedures.

Key Performance Indicators:

  • Strategy Execution
  • Employee Engagement
  • Budget Plan vs Expenditure
  • Talent Attraction, Acquisition, Development, and Retention
  • Employee Engagement

Experience and Qualifications Required:

  • Master’s degree in organizational psychology, Human Resources, Business Administration, or a relevant field will be an added advantage
  • Minimum of 7 years of working experience in human resources management with 3 years human resource senior management role.
