Job Description

This description has been adapted for JobNziza readers to provide a clearer overview of the opportunity.

Job Title: Customer Service Agent

Department: Communications

Location: AC Mobility Offices, Kigali - Rwanda

Modality: Full-Time

Contract Duration: One Year

Contract Type: Fixed Term

Reporting Structure:

Direct Supervisor/Reports To: Head of Communications

Works Closely With: Solutions assist Associate

Role Overview

As the Customer Service Agent, you are tasked with providing timely, professional, and empathetic frontline assistance to AC Mobility customers across all customer-care touchpoints. The role serves as a primary point of contact for commuter enquiries, complaints, and service requests, ensuring accurate information is provided, resolving standard issues at the first point of contact, and properly documenting and escalating complex cases requiring technical or operational investigation.

Core Responsibility

To deliver customers with a reliable, reassuring, and positive assist experience by understanding their needs, delivering accurate information, achieving high first-contact resolution on routine enquiries, and ensuring unresolved issues are documented and routed efficiently through established escalation pathways.

Key Responsibilities

  • Frontline Customer assist: Receive, manage, and resolve incoming customer enquiries and complaints professionally, courteously, and empathetically.
  • Customer Information Delivery: deliver clear, precise, and up-to-date guidance regarding AC Mobility products, Tap&Go fare structures, card usage, and service procedures.
  • First Contact Resolution (FCR): Resolve routine, frequently occurring customer enquiries (such as balance queries, basic card issues, and system guidance) during the initial interaction.
  • Complaint Handling and De-escalation: Actively listen to customer grievances, defuse tense interactions with composure, and deliver appropriate assistance while upholding professional standards.
  • Follow-up and Communication: Contact commuters to deliver progress updates, request additional information, or confirm the successful resolution of reported issues.
  • CRM and Case Management: Accurately record, categorise, and oversee all customer interactions, service requests, and feedback within the company’s CRM and ticketing systems.
  • Tier-2 Escalation: Accurately document and escalate technical faults, transactional discrepancies, or operational challenges to the Solutions assist Associate in line with standard operating procedures.
  • Customer Feedback Logging: Systematically detect and flag recurring commuter pain points, agent network issues, or validator failure patterns to supervisory and technical teams.
  • Data Security and Confidentiality: keep absolute discretion and protect sensitive commuter identity, card data, and transaction histories in strict adherence to data protection standards.
  • Continuous Learning and Compliance: keep a thorough understanding of AC Mobility platforms, updates, workflows, and assigned shift rotas.

Working Relationship with the Solutions assist Associate

The Customer Service Agent provides Tier-1 frontline assist, handling initial commuter engagements and resolving routine queries using documented procedures.

Where an issue requires technical diagnosis, backend transaction verification, or cross-departmental coordination, the Agent documents the case and formally escalates it to the Solutions assist Associate.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • First Contact Resolution (FCR): Achieve ≥80% resolution rate on standard enquiries during the first interaction.
  • Response and Resolution Timelines: Adhere strictly to agreed customer response and ticket resolution times across all live assist channels.
  • Customer Satisfaction (CSAT): keep a positive customer satisfaction rating of ≥85% based on post-interaction feedback.
  • CRM Record Accuracy: 100% of customer interactions accurately tagged, documented, and categorised with zero critical omissions.
  • Escalation Accuracy: Zero critical misroutings of technical or operational tickets escalated to the Solutions assist Associate.
  • Schedule Adherence: High punctuality and compliance with allocated shift rotas and operational breaks.

Performance Evaluation and Terms

Performance in this role will be continuously evaluated to ensure against customer care benchmarks, response accuracy, and adherence to operational standards.

Ramifications of Underperformance:

Expectations for this role are high, reflecting its importance to the organisation's overall success. A sustained failure to achieve Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), fulfil core responsibilities, or uphold AC Mobility’s standards of professional perform will trigger a formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). Inability to demonstrate the required improvement within the stipulated timeframe may result in the termination of employment.

Qualifications and Core Competencies

1. Educational Background

  • Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Customer Care, Communications, Public Relations, Business Administration, or a related field.

2. Professional Experience

  • Prior customer-facing or call centre experience within technology, telecommunications, financial services, or transport environments is an added advantage.

3. Language Proficiency

  • Fluency in Kinyarwanda and English is required; working knowledge of French is an added advantage.

4. Professional Certifications

  • Preferred:
  • Certified Customer Service Professional (CCSP) or Customer Service Excellence Certification (CSEC): Demonstrates mastery of foundational service principles, complaint resolution, and front-facing relationship management.
  • Help Desk Institute (HDI) assist Center Analyst: Validates best-practice competencies in multi-channel ticket logging, service desk workflows, and issue escalation.
  • ITIL Foundation (v4): Recommended for agents operating alongside technical teams to understand incident ticketing, service level agreements (SLAs), and change escalation procedures.
  • CRM Platform Certifications: Practical product badges or credentials in industry-standard ticketing and CRM suites (such as Zendesk, HubSpot Service Hub, or Salesforce Service Cloud).

5. Additional Hard Competencies

  • CRM and Ticketing Systems: Competence in logging, categorising, and tracking tickets within enterprise CRM or customer assist software.
  • Digital Literacy: Comfort working across multiple web applications, digital mobility tools, and office productivity platforms with high typing speed and accuracy.
  • Product Literacy: Comprehensive understanding of cashless payment flows, bus ticketing workflows, and Tap&Go operational rules.

Soft Competencies

Command of key competencies needed for the modern workplace, including but not limited to: Strategic Leadership, High-Level Problem Solving, Critical Thinking, Uncompromising Integrity, Excellent Cross-Functional Communication, Work Ethic, Dependability, Empathy, Professionalism, and effective Stress Management in high-stakes environments.

In addition:

  • Customer-Centric Communication: Active listening and clear, professional verbal and written expression across diverse commuter demographics.
  • Emotional Resilience and De-escalation: Proven ability to remain calm, patient, and polite when managing difficult situations or high-volume peak periods.
  • Attention to Detail and Accuracy: Rigour in recording accurate ticket details, capturing caller data, and relaying factual procedural information.
  • Dependability and Process Discipline: Strict adherence to shift rosters, attendance guidelines, SOPs, and tiered escalation matrices.
  • Ethical perform and Discretion: Absolute integrity and responsible handling of private commuter and transaction records.

What We Offer

AC Mobility offers a vibrant, purpose-driven workplace at the forefront of East Africa’s cashless transit revolution. As a Customer Service Agent, you will join a supportive, collaborative Communications and Customer Care team dedicated to delivering world-class service to millions of daily commuters. We offer competitive compensation packages, comprehensive health insurance coverage, structured shift patterns, continuous professional coaching in modern CRM platforms and conflict de-escalation, and clear internal career progression pathways into technical assist, operations, or supervisory roles within the organisation.

JOB ADVERTISEMENT:

Impanuro Girls Initiative (IGI) is seeking to recruit a “Leathercraft and Crafting Teacher”.

Introduction

IMPANURO is a Kinyarwanda word that translates as "good advice" or "guidance." Impanuro Girls’ Initiative (IGI) is a young women-led national non-governmental organization legally registered and authorized to operate in Rwanda. As a nonprofit organization, IGI fosters women's empowerment and builds girls' agency under registration number N° 763/RGB/NGO/LP/11/2021 issued by the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB). The founder of the organization was determined to address teenage pregnancy issues resulting from poor or no access to Sexual Reproductive Health (SRH) information and services, among other systemic challenges.

Our Values: PASSION, HUMANITY, ACCOUNTABILITY, and INTEGRITY.

Our Mission: We are a young women-led Rwandan non-governmental organization, striving to enhance women and girls’ lives through education, capacity building, counselling, socio-economic empowerment, and advocacy to ensure a healthy and dignified lifestyle.

Our Vision: A Rwandan society where women and girls have healthy and dignified lives, are meaningfully engaged in communities and are economically empowered.

About the Role

The Leathercraft and Crafting Teacher will deliver 6 months of comprehensive, highly practical instruction to students at the IGI Ruhango Tekena Hub using dedicated inventory assets. Your objective is to train students in the integrated processes of leather footwear production, artisanal design, and contemporary handcrafting, equipping young women to launch self-reliant micro-enterprises, footwear workshops, or creative craft brands, while supporting each trainee's confidence, voice, and economic empowerment. Training follows the RTB-accredited 6-month curriculum, including competency-based assessment, trainee portfolios, and supervision of the 2-month Industrial Attachment Program. This position works closely with both the Field guide and Center Coordinator.

Who The organization is seeking:

Education Qualifications

Education: Diploma or Certificate in Leather Technology, Footwear Production, Fine Arts, Industrial Art and Design, or a related composite TVET qualification.

Certification: TVET teacher certification or formal pedagogical training endorsement.

Experiences:

2–3 years of verifiable experience operating an active footwear manufacturing workshop, custom leather goods company, or commercial craft collective.

Expert proficiency across shoe lasting methodologies, mechanical operation of heavy leather machines, hand tools, precise fabric/leather nesting, and diverse traditional African weaving patterns (such as Agaseke).

RTB-registered Trainer/Assessor status or Trainer of Trainers (ToT) certificate is an added advantage; valid Police Clearance/Criminal Record Certificate required prior to appointment.

LANGUAGES

Candidates must be Complete fluency in Kinyarwanda.

Professional working proficiency in English and/or French is a strong advantage.

greatrwandajobs.title: Agronomist job at Fisher Global Ltd
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background information about the job or company (e.g., role context, company overview)

Fisher Global Ltd is a Rwandan agribusiness and diversified business company established in 2016, with a strong focus on sustainable agriculture, agricultural production, processing, export, logistics, and international trade. The company is committed to contributing to Rwanda’s economic development by connecting high-quality Rwandan agricultural products to local and international markets while creating sustainable economic opportunities for farmers and rural communities.

Fisher Global’s core agricultural activities include the commercial production and aggregation of chilli, soybeans, maize, and other high-value crops, complemented by agronomic assist, farm management, post-harvest handling, warehousing, and export services. The company has developed particular expertise in the chilli value chain, including the production, processing, quality management, packaging, and export of dried chilli products to international markets.

Fisher Global Ltd is expanding its agricultural and post-harvest operations and invites applications from qualified, motivated, and results-oriented candidates for the following positions:

AGRONOMIST

The Agronomist will deliver technical and field-level assist to ensure improved crop productivity, quality, sustainability, and compliance with Good Agricultural Practices (GAP). The successful candidate will work closely with farmers, field teams, and other stakeholders to assist crop production and achieve Fisher Global Ltd’s agricultural objectives.

Responsibilities or duties

  • Deliver technical advice on crop production, soil fertility, irrigation, fertilizer application, pest and disease management, and crop protection.
  • Perform regular farm visits to track crop performance and detect production challenges.
  • Train farmers and field teams on modern farming technologies and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP).
  • Perform field demonstrations, farmer training, and extension activities.
  • Assist out-growers and partner farmers with technical assistance.
  • Track crop establishment, growth, harvesting, and overall production performance.
  • Collect field data and assist yield estimation and production forecasting.
  • Track proper use of agricultural inputs and compliance with company production standards.
  • Assist food safety, traceability, certification, environmental, and sustainability requirements.

Fisher Global Ltd is a Rwandan agribusiness and diversified business company established in 2016, with a strong focus on sustainable agriculture, agricultural production, processing, export, logistics, and international trade. DRYING SITE OFFICER

The Drying Site Officer will oversee post-harvest activities including the receiving, inspection, drying, sorting, grading, processing, and storage of agricultural products such as chili (urusenda), rosemary, and other crops.

The successful candidate will be tasked with maintaining product quality, reducing post harvest losses, ensuring food safety, and supporting efficient movement of produce from collection points through processing and storage.

  • Receive and inspect agricultural produce from farmers and collection points.

  • Track processing output, product losses, stock levels, and quality performance.
  • Keep accurate daily, weekly, and monthly records and reports.
  • Assist product traceability and certification requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with food safety, hygiene, workplace safety, and environmental standards.
  • Organize with Field Officers, Logistics, Quality Control, and Operations teams.
  • Report equipment breakdowns, quality issues, losses, and other operational challenges promptly.
  • Assist harvesting and post-harvest planning and schedules.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Diploma (A2) in Agriculture, or Bachelor’s Degree in Food Science, Agribusiness, Post Harvest Technology, or a related field.
  • Having 1–2 years of relevant experience in post-harvest handling, food processing, drying operations, agribusiness, or warehouse operations will be an additional advantage.
  • Experience with drying systems, food processing equipment, or warehouse management is an advantage.
  • Knowledge of food safety, hygiene, quality control, and post-harvest loss reduction.
  • Basic computer skills for reporting and record keeping.
  • Strong organizational and operational skills.
  • Attention to detail and commitment to product quality.
  • Good teamwork and communication skills.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
  • High level of integrity, accountability, and responsibility.

  • Strong work ethic and professional integrity.

greatrwandajobs.description:
About University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)

University of Global Health Equity is a health sciences university in Rwanda. An initiative of Partners In Health, UGHE is a private, not-for-profit, accredited institution

About This Opportunity

The position of Biobank Coordinator (Administrative & Research Operations) at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE) located in Burera, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

Description

Position Title: Biobank Coordinator (Administrative & Research Operations)

Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER)

Reports To: Head of Biobank

Location: Kigali with regular travel to research sites

Contract Duration: Two year contract with possible extension for another two years

Position Summary

The Biobank coordinator will deliver operational, administrative, and research coordination assist for biobank activities and clinical trial projects. The position will ensure effective planning, implementation, documentation, and monitoring of research activities while maintaining compliance with institutional policies, ethical requirements, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and biobank quality standards.

The Coordinator will serve as a key liaison between investigators, clinical trial teams, laboratory personnel, research participants, regulatory bodies, and collaborating institutions. The role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, experience in research administration, and the ability to organize multiple activities simultaneously.

Key Responsibilities

  • organize daily biobank operations, including specimen collection, processing, storage, tracking, inventory, access, documentation, and compliance.
  • assist clinical trial implementation, including timelines, regulatory documentation, site coordination, monitoring visits, recruitment tracking, essential documents, and logistics.
  • organize research activities, work plans, meetings, reports, budgets, procurement, travel, and project documentation.
  • Ensure adherence to GCP, ethics and regulatory requirements, biobank policies, data protection, and assist audits and accreditation activities.
  • Serve as a coordination point among investigators, clinical teams, laboratory/biobank staff, sponsors, regulators, and research partners, ensuring effective communication and follow-up.

Required Qualifications and competence

  • Bachelor’s degree in Health/Biomedical/Laboratory Sciences, Public Health, Clinical Research, Life Sciences, Health Administration, or related field; Master’s degree is an advantage.
  • Experience: 3–5 years’ experience in clinical research, clinical trials, biobanking, laboratory research, or research administration.

Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER)

Duty Station: UGHE-AVEGA Biobank and UGHE, Kigali. Frequent travel to the Butaro campus, Northern Province, Burera District, Rwanda

Position Summary

The Biobank Head provides strategic, scientific, technical, and operational leadership for the establishment and management of the UGHE-AVEGA Biobank, a core research infrastructure of the Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER). The position is tasked with leading the planning, establishment, operationalization, accreditation, and continuous improvement of the biobank to assist clinical trials, translational research, precision medicine, genomics, oncology, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and population health research.

The Head is tasked with the overall administration and day-to-day management of biobank operations, including biospecimen acquisition, processing, storage, inventory management, retrieval, distribution, Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) administration, quality management systems, biosafety and biosecurity, regulatory compliance, equipment management, financial oversight, and supervision of biobank personnel.

The Biobank Head will play a pivotal leadership role in developing institutional policies, standard operating procedures, governance frameworks, regulatory systems, quality assurance programs, and strategic partnerships that ensure the biobank operates in accordance with ISBER Best Practices, ISO 20387, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and all applicable national and international regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • guide the establishment and operation of the UGHE–AVEGA Biobank and align activities with UGHE/IGHER priorities.
  • Establish SOPs, Quality Management Systems, governance, and regulatory compliance, including preparation for ISO 20387 accreditation and ISBER Best Practices.
  • guide implementation and management of the LIMS and ensure secure, accurate, and traceable data management.
  • Oversee biospecimen management, quality, traceability, security, staffing, equipment, budgets, and daily operations.
  • Integrate biobanking with clinical trials and research programs and create national and international collaborations.
  • Build staff capacity through training, mentorship, and competency development in biobanking, GCP/GCLP, biosafety, and quality management.

Qualifications

Education

  • PhD (preferred) or Master's in Biobanking, Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biomedical/Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Pathology, Genomics, Public Health, Clinical Research, or related field. Certification in GCLP, GCP, ISO 20387, ISO 15189, ISBER Best Practices, or QMS/Laboratory Management is a plus.

Experience

  • 8+ years in biobank management, biomedical research, clinical laboratory management, or clinical trial assist, including 5+ years in senior leadership supervising multidisciplinary teams
  • Proven track record establishing or expanding a biobank/biospecimen repository — infrastructure planning, workflow development, and operations
  • Experience implementing LIMS and laboratory/biobank Quality Management Systems
  • Hands-on management of biospecimen collection, processing, cryopreservation, storage, and distribution
  • Equipment lifecycle management (procurement through calibration/maintenance)
  • Experience managing donor-funded programs, budgets, and strategic/donor reporting
  • Developed SOPs, quality manuals, and governance structures (Oversight/Scientific Advisory/Data Access Committees)
  • Prepared labs for ISO 20387, ISO 15189, or ISBER accreditation; built CAPA and audit systems
  • Prepared IRB/ethics/regulatory documentation; ensured compliance with biospecimen collection, storage, and export regulations
  • Developed informed consent, data privacy, and biobank governance frameworks
  • Supported regulatory inspections and audits
  • Strong command of ISBER, ISO 20387/15189, GCLP/GCP, LIMS, and biosafety/QMS standards. Excellent leadership, project and financial management, and scientific writing/communication skills.
  • Experience establishing a national/regional biobank; integrating biobanking into clinical trials; working with international institutions or in LMIC/Africa settings; PMP/PRINCE2 certification; strong publication and grant-management record.

greatrwandajobs.title: Agronomist - FXBVILLAGE Project job at FXB Rwanda
greatrwandajobs.description:
About FXB Rwanda

FXB Rwanda is a registered Rwandan Local Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) rooted in Rwanda since 1995, and a member of FXB Global, carrying the legacy of François-Xavier Bagnoud into its fourth decade — across all four provinces and the City of Kigali.

FXB Rwanda implements integrated development programs aimed at reducing poverty and vulnerability and promoting sustainable livelihoods, food and nutrition security, health, education, WASH, and economic empowerment.

FXB Rwanda is currently seeking to recruit a qualified, motivated, and experienced Agronomist to assist the implementation of the FXBVillage Project in Gisagara District.

Position Information

Job Title: Agronomist

Project: FXBVillage Project

Duty Station: Gisagara District, Rwanda

Reports to: Program Coordinator

Employment Type: Fixed-term contract – 12 months, renewable subject to performance

Expected Start Date: October 2026

Project Background

The FXBVillage program uses a holistic approach designed to addresses the multiple interconnected dimensions of poverty, including health, education, and income generation, to help the most vulnerable families become self-sufficient and graduate out of extreme poverty within a three-year period. From October 2026, FXB Rwanda will start the implementation of the FXBVillage project in Kansi and Kibirizi sectors of Gisagara District in the Southern Province of Rwanda.

Job Purpose

The Agronomist will deliver technical guidance and hands-on assist to FXBVillage participant households to enhance agricultural productivity, food and nutrition security, household income, and resilience to climate change.

The position will assist participants to adopt regenerative and climate-resilient agricultural practices, enhance soil health, increase crop productivity and quality, strengthen sustainable farming systems, and link farmers to appropriate markets.

Low-tech solutions and regenerative agriculture practices will be implemented through two complementary levels of Climate-Resilient and Regenerative Agriculture Hubs (CRRAHs). Community CRRAHs will serve as collective learningand demonstration spaces incorporating agroforestry, fruit trees, composting, organic fertilizers, local food preservation techniques, rainwater harvesting, as well as the promotion, propagation, and conservation of local seeds adapted to the agroecological realities of the project areas.

The successful candidate will work closely with participant households, community structures, local authorities, and other agricultural stakeholders to make sure that project-supported agricultural interventions are effectively implemented and generate sustainable results.

A. Key Duties and Responsibilities

1. Agricultural Technical assist and Extension

  • deliver technical guidance and practical coaching to participant households on crop production and sustainable agricultural practices.
  • Train farmers on appropriate crop selection, seasonal planning, land preparation, planting, crop management, harvesting, post-harvest handling, and storage.
  • Promote the adoption of regenerative and climate-resilient agriculture practices, including soil fertility management, erosion control, water conservation, crop diversification, mulching, composting, agroecological practices, and other appropriate techniques.
  • assist farmers to enhance soil health, productivity, and the sustainable use of available land and natural resources.
  • perform regular field visits throughout the agricultural cycle, from land preparation and planting through harvesting, to deliver timely technical advice.
  • detect agricultural challenges affecting participant households and deliver appropriate technical solutions.

2. Farmer Training and Demonstration

  • Contribute to the design and adaptation of agriculture related training manuals.
  • Design and facilitate practical agricultural training sessions for participant households .
  • Establish and facilitate Climate-Resilient and Regenerative Agriculture Hubs (CRRAHs) and practical demonstration plots where appropriate.
  • Facilitate farmer-led experimentation and learning to detect locally appropriate and effective agricultural practices.
  • Promote peer-to-peer learning and knowledge sharing among participant farmers.
  • assist farmers to apply improved technologies, including Water Harvesting techniques and farming practices demonstrated through the project.

3. Agricultural Productivity and Food Security

  • assist participant households to increase crop productivity, enhance the quality of agricultural produce, and strengthen household food security.
  • Promote diversified agricultural production to enhance household nutrition and resilience.
  • Advise farmers on efficient and sustainable use of agricultural inputs and resources.
  • assist participants to create practical agricultural production plans aligned with local seasons, market opportunities, and household priorities.

4. Market Linkages and Income Generation

  • Facilitate linkages between farmers, cooperatives, buyers, local markets, and other relevant value-chain actors.
  • deliver guidance on post-harvest handling, quality improvement, aggregation, and value addition.
  • detect opportunities for participants to strengthen agriculture-based income-generating activities.

5. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Work closely with Sector and District agricultural officers and agronomists in the planning and implementation of project agricultural activities.
  • keep effective collaboration with local authorities, farmer groups, cooperatives, extension workers, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Participate in relevant agricultural meetings, workshops, trainings, and coordination forums on behalf of FXB Rwanda, as assigned.
  • Ensure effective coordination between agricultural interventions and other components of the FXBVillage Project.

B. Required Qualifications and Competencies

1. Education and Professional Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Agronomy, Agriculture, Crop Production, Agricultural Sciences, or another closely related field.
  • At least three (3) years of relevant professional experience in agronomy, agricultural extension, crop production. Working with smallholder farmers and rural communities will be an added advantage.
  • Demonstrated practical experience in regenerative agriculture, climate-resilient agriculture, sustainable land management, or agroecological practices is highly desirable.
  • Experience working with NGOs, community-based programs, or development projects will be an added advantage.
  • Experience facilitating farmer training, demonstration plots, farmer learning groups, or similar community-based agricultural approaches is an advantage.

2. Technical and Personal Competencies

  • Strong knowledge of regenerative and climate-resilient agriculture practices.
  • Practical understanding of crop production and smallholder farming systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with rural communities and vulnerable households.
  • Strong facilitation, coaching, and community mobilization skills.
  • Good communication, interpersonal, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Strong organizational, planning, problem-solving, and reporting skills.
  • Good analytical and field-level monitoring skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Fluency in Kinyarwanda is required; good working knowledge of English and/or French is an advantage.
  • A valid Category A driving license (motorcycle) is required, as the position involves regular field travel to rural communities and participant households.
  • Willingness and ability to work extensively in the field and travel within Gisagara District.

C. Gender and Inclusion

Female candidates are particularly encouraged to apply and will be given additional consideration.

Ubuyobozi bwa UFACO Garments Ltd buramenyesha ababyeyi, urubyiruko ndetse n’abandi bose bifuza kwiga umwuga wo kudoda, ko bwafunguye gahunda y’amahugurwa y’igihe gito mu mwuga wo kudoda no gukora imyenda (Garment Making / Tailoring).

Amahugurwa azamara igihe kingana n’amezi atandatu (6 months), kandi abazayitabira baziga biyishyurira. Muri aya mahugurwa, abanyeshuri bazahabwa ubumenyi n’ubushobozi mu bikorwa birimo:

  • Gukoresha imashini zitandukanye zidoda;
  • Kumenya ibikoresho n’imyenda ikoreshwa mu kudoda;
  • Gupima no gufata ibipimo by’imyenda;
  • Gukata imyenda hakurikijwe ibipimo;
  • Kudoda no guteranya ibice by’imyenda;
  • Gukora amashati, amapantalo, amakanzu n’indi myambaro;
  • Gukora finishing no kugenzura ubuziranenge bw’imyenda;

Amahugurwa ngiro (practical training) azakorerwa muri UFACO Garments Ltd kugira ngo abanyeshuri babone ubumenyi bushingiye ku kazi gakorerwa mu ruganda.

IBISABWA KU BASHAKA KWIYANDIKISHA

  • Kuba bafite ubushake bwo kwiga umwuga wo kudoda;
  • Kuzana fotokopi y’Indangamuntu cyangwa ikindi cyangombwa kibanga;
  • Kuzana fotokopi y’impamyabumenyi ku bayifite;
  • Kuzuza ifishi yo kwiyandikisha;
  • Kwemera gukurikiza gahunda n’abwiriza agenga amahugurwa;
  • Kwishyura amafaranga y’amahugurwa nk’uko azagenwa na UFACO Garments Ltd.

IGIHE AMAHUGURWA AZAMARA

NB1: Amasomo azamara amezi atandatu (6) kandi azibanda cyane ku myitozo ngiro, kugira ngo uyasoje abe ashoboye gukoresha neza imashini zidoda no gukora imyenda ku rwego rw’umwuga, ku buryo ashobora kwihangira umurimo cyangwa gukorera mu nganda zikora imyenda. Abazaba barangije neza aya mahugurwa bazahabwa icyemezo (Certificate) cyemewe kandi kiriho umukono wa RTB (Rwanda TVET Board), ikigo cya Leta gifite inshingano zo guteza imbere no kugenzura imyigishirize y’imyuga n’ubumenyingiro mu Rwanda.

NB2: Itariki yo gutangira amasomo, ndetse n’andi makuru yose ajyanye n’amahugurwa bizamenyeshwa gusa abamaze kwiyandikisha. Amasomo azajya atangira mu gitondo kugeza saa munani z’amanywa (14:00). Abifuza kwiyandikisha basabwe kohereza ibyangombwa bisabwa nk’uko byavuzwe haruguru kuri izi aderesi za email: info@ufaco.top copy to agathe.nyirashimiyimana@ufaco.top. Kwiyandikisha bizarangira ku wa 30/09/2026.

greatrwandajobs.title: Project Manager job at Raising The Village
greatrwandajobs.description:
About Raising The Village

At Raising The Village (RTV), we are dedicated to eradicating ultra-poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact.To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

Position Summary

The Project Manager plays a critical role in overseeing the successful implementation of multiple projects within a district, ensuring alignment with RTV’s strategic goals, project designs, and work plans. This role involves providing strong leadership, mentorship, and operational support to Team Leads and Officers, ensuring they have the necessary resources, guidance, and capacity to execute projects effectively.

In addition to people and team management, the Project Manager is responsible for office administration and operations, fostering an environment where teams are fully supported to meet program objectives. They serve as the key liaison between staff, government counterparts and management, proactively addressing challenges, streamlining processes, and ensuring smooth communication and workflow across all levels.

The ideal candidate is a results-oriented leader with strong experience in coaching and managing teams, mobilizing and coordinating with government institutions, and delivering complex, multi-sector projects in rural contexts. They are solutions-driven, highly organized, and committed to building high-performing teams that deliver sustainable, government-aligned impact for communities served by RTV. Note: The Project Manager may be based at a District Government Office and embedded with government teams to foster collaboration and strengthen partnerships.

Government & Community Coordination and assist

  • Work closely with community leadership and assist structures including Inteko z’abaturage, Incuti z’umuryango, Abajyanama b’Ubuzima, Abajyanama b’Ubuhinzi (farmer promoters), para-social workers, community coaches, technical and village coaches, and other community actors to ensure their active participation in RTV programs.

  • deliver on-the-job assist and follow-up to community and government actors during implementation to help address challenges and encourage consistent participation.
  • Promote positive collaboration and trust between RTV staff, government officials, and community structures to strengthen community ownership and contribute to sustainable program impact.

Reporting and Administration

  • create and oversee work plans;
  • Complete field reporting on a weekly basis and deliver assist with information sharing for donor reporting and proposal writing as might be required;

  • deliver suggestions to management on potential activities that need to be redone, reviewed or introduced to ensure sustainability of RTV projects, methodologies, and improvement in the lives of community members.

  • Bachelor’s degree in agriculture is preferred but not required

  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written English;

  • Able to keep a positive attitude in a fast-paced and challenging environment;
  • Energetic and physically able to hike high to hike high terrain;
  • Able to travel approximately 90% of time;
  • Ability to ride a motorbike with a valid Rwandan rider’s permit (class A) and demonstrated experience navigating remote, rural and hilly terrain (mandatory).

greatrwandajobs.description:
VisionFund Rwanda (VFR), is Rwanda’s largest microfinance Institution. VFR is committed to the development of Rwanda through providing affordable financial services (savings and loans) to the less privileged throughout its 4 zones in Rwanda.

VFR is the institution where you can develop your expertise working with the best people worldwide in a dynamic, team focused high performance environment. If you are looking for interesting but challenging work where you can make a difference in the world, then VFR has the will to make it so.

VisionFund Rwanda (VFR) has zero tolerance to abuse and sexual exploitation of children and adults beneficiaries. We expect all our employees/affiliates to commit to protecting children and adult beneficiaries from harm and abide by our safeguarding policy.

JOB SUMMARY

The establishment of the digital project manager function is to drive delivery of digitalization initiatives and maximize benefits of digital solutions within Vision Fund Rwanda and by extension aid in achieving Vision Funds’ International digitalization strategy.

The Digital Project Manager (DPM), as an independent and focused role, will oversee the portfolio of identified digitalization projects with the main focus of driving paperless and cashless expectations. The person is to manage the digital projects life cycle from pre-project to closure.

Responsibilities or duties

Key responsibilities and weighting (adds to 100%)

  • (20%) VFR digital strategy and innovation
    • In charge of VFR digital strategy and road map
    • Work with SLT to map out the VFR digital strategy road map and plan for its evolution
    • Lead VFR digital innovation - identify areas of improvements, give and seek ideas on process improvement and follow through their implementation
    • Ensure that digitization translates to real benefits to VFR and its clients
  • (30%) Digital project management
    • Planning, Organizing, Monitoring and control of project deliverables.
    • Leading and coordinating all project implementation activities while adhering to specifications, and time and cost estimates.
    • Project Documentation: Business case, Functional specification documents, Project plans (on smart sheets), Project Contracts, Business Process Documentation, updating of SOPS and policies relating to digital changes, training manuals, STC minutes, Post implementation reports.
  • (25%) Change management
    • Ensures VFR staff are ready for change. Communicates the urgency to go digital across all our operations by year 2030. Breaks down the why, how and when of the digital strategy.
    • Ensures all internal and external customers are well trained and have what they need for a successful roll out.
    • Ensure that users properly test the digital solutions to ensure it meets business acceptance criteria for deployment.
    • In charge of the go to market strategy: Ensures successful roll out of digital solutions across VFR and to customers.
  • (20%) Digital projects reporting
    • Track and communicate project status to stakeholders (CEO, COO/HOIT and Regional Project Manager) on a weekly basis. Reporting progress to the VFR project STC.
    • Manage digital project issue risks during all project phases, flag escalate blockages and seek solutions in collaboration with all stakeholders.
    • Track digital projects expenditure and share the quarterly spend with relevant stakeholders.
    • Track digital projects KPIs post go live and ensure the business achieves the benefits highlighted in the business case.
    • Carry out project post implementation review 6 months after go live - document lessons and recommend enhancements.
  • (5%) Spirituality
    • Supportive and exemplifying role model that upholds Christian Values and Principles. Regularly attend the staff spiritual and nurture activities.
    • Maintain a positive working relationship with all staff, provide clear written and verbal communication and acquire and develop professional skills that benefit VisionFund.

Qualifications or requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Business or IT or in a field relevant to project management.

Good communication and presentation skills; fluency in English is an advantage

Experience needed

  • Three years’ experience managing complex software implementations (preferably financial systems)
  • Three years of general project management experience across multiple functions.
  • Proven ability to self-manage and use conventional project management tools and techniques.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Preferable Project management certifications in PMP, PRINCE, Business Analysis or Six Sigma
  • Recent technical training on Project management.
  • Determined personality with initiative, perseverance and the ability to motivate and manage a team.
  • Capability and willingness to take responsibility and highly developed sense of rectitude
  • Ready to comply and live up to and in accordance with the organization Ideals and Core Values,
  • Be proficient in Microsoft office applications,
  • Good knowledge in economic and financial topics,
  • Be a good trainer, facilitator, mentor, and coach
  • Very good communication and marketing skills
  • A mature, committed Christian

Working Environment / Conditions:

  • Office environment: typical office based 60% and field 40%
  • Travel: 80% Domestic/ 20% international travel is required.
  • On call: (in the after normal working hours)

Our offer

VisionFund Rwanda is willing to offer you a competitive salary, challenging work where you can make a difference in the world, develop your expertise by working with the best people worldwide in a dynamic, team focused and high performing environment

greatrwandajobs.title: Expression Of Interest For a Company To Conduct A Scoping Study tender at Trinity Musha Mines Ltd
greatrwandajobs.description:
Expression Of Interest For a Company To Conduct A Scoping Study Tender at Trinity Metals Limited

Trinity Metals Limited invites your organizations to submit an Expression of Interest (“EOI”) to be considered for appointment as Lead Consultant to undertake an independent Scoping Study of the Rutongo Mine (Rulindo District, Northern Province) Republic of Rwanda. Rutongo comprises six historical mining areas (Gisanze, Masoro, Nyamyumba, Gasambya, Karambo, and Mahaza) on the Rutongo anticline, mining cassiterite hosted in steeply-dipping quartz veins, with existing processing plants at Nyamyumba and Karambo. Unlike Musha, mineralisation at Rutongo is tin-only, with no material tantalum or lithium credit. Rutongo's own published materials describe an already-mechanised operation with an established reserve base (in the order of 54,000 t recoverable tin); however, Trinity's working characterisation for this Study is that Rutongo remains semi-artisanal in material respects (mine development, grade control, and stockpile treatment). Reconciling these two positions, using independently verified data, is itself a required output of this Study for Rutongo (see Section 6.4.1 and 6.4.2). Given the number and scale of these areas, each of the six areas — including the condition, capacity, and continued suitability of the existing Nyamyumba and Karambo plants — shall first be assessed individually (own resource estimate, mine plan, and metallurgical performance where data allows) before being consolidated into a single, overall Rutongo development case that captures sequencing, shared infrastructure, and blending opportunities across areas.

Trinity currently operates the Mine on a semi-artisanal basis. The purpose of the Scoping Study is to assess the technical and economic potential to develop the Mine into a formalised, mechanized operation, and to provide Trinity's Board and investors with a credible basis for further investment decisions, including whether to proceed to a Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS).

Scope of Work: 

Stage 0 — Data Review and Fatal-Flaw Assessment (Gate)

Objective

To review and validate the geological, survey, production, metallurgical, environmental, and cost information currently available for Rutongo Mines; to confirm what can reasonably be relied upon for the purposes of this Study and what requires independent re-verification; to confirm whether representative samples can be obtained to support Stage 1 testwork; and to identify any material fatal flaw — in Mineral Resource, mining, processing, permitting, social, or infrastructure terms — before significant testwork or study expenditure is committed.

Activities

  • compile and critically review all available geological, survey, production, metallurgical, environmental, and cost data and records for the Mine, including the 2018 AMS study to the extent it applies, and record the provenance, vintage, and reliability of each data set;
  • inspect and report on the condition of existing workings and access (declines, shafts, haul roads, and surface infrastructure), and validate existing mine survey control and as-built records against physical conditions on site;
  • confirm whether representative samples of current ore, development material, and legacy stockpiled/tailings material can practicably be obtained to support the Stage 1 metallurgical testwork programme;
  • review relevant lessons learned from Trinity's Nyakabingo plant design and tailings storage facility (TSF) trade-off study (to be made available by Trinity) and identify implications for processing and tailings planning at this Mine;
  • identify and assess material fatal-flaw risks across Mineral Resource, mining, processing, permitting/regulatory, social, and infrastructure disciplines; and
  • prepare a data-gap register benchmarked against Scoping Study-level requirements (see Annex B), together with a costed, time-bound plan to close priority gaps before or during Stage 1 and Stage 2.

Deliverables

  • Data Review and Fatal-Flaw Assessment Report, including a clear statement of what data can reasonably be relied upon and what cannot;
  • Data-Gap Register, ranked by criticality, with a costed and time-bound plan to close priority gaps; and
  • Stage 0 Gate Review Memorandum with a clear recommendation (proceed to Stage 1 / proceed subject to conditions / do not proceed) and supporting rationale.

Gate Criteria

Trinity regards Stage 0 as the most important gate in this Study: its purpose is to protect Trinity from committing significant testwork or study expenditure against incomplete or unreliable inputs. The Consultant shall propose, for Trinity's agreement during mobilisation, gate criteria covering as a minimum: (i) no unmitigated fatal flaw has been identified at Rutongo Mines that would preclude further study expenditure; (ii) a clear, agreed, and costed plan exists to close any critical data gaps before or during Stage 1 and Stage 2; and (iii) representative sampling for Stage 1 metallurgical testwork is confirmed as achievable. These criteria, once agreed, will govern the go/no-go decision at the end of Stage 0. Trinity retains sole approval authority over this and every subsequent gate (Section 8).

Stage 1 — Metallurgical Testwork and Characterisation (Gate)

Objective

Contingent on Rutongo Mines having satisfied its Stage 0 gate (or an agreed mitigation permitting progression), to determine, on the basis of representative sampling and laboratory/pilot-scale testwork, whether ore from Rutongo Mines (and, where relevant, legacy stockpiled or tailings material) can be economically upgraded to a saleable concentrate meeting market specification, at what recovery and grade, and by what practicable flowsheet.

Activities

  • design the metallurgical testwork programme, informed by the Stage 0 data review and by consultation with Trinity's site personnel;
  • design and execute a representative sampling programme covering current run-of-mine ore, development ore, and legacy stockpiled/tailings material, with documented QA/QC;
  • undertake mineralogical characterisation (liberation, association, and gangue mineralogy of cassiterite);
  • undertake comminution characterisation (e.g. Bond work index or equivalent) sufficient for scoping-level equipment sizing;
  • undertake beneficiation testwork appropriate to cassiterite mineralisation (typically gravity-based methods such as jigging, spirals, and shaking tables), including assessment of upgrading opportunities relative to current recovery practice;
  • determine achievable recovery and concentrate grade against current market/offtake specification for tin (cassiterite), including conflict-free/ITSCI chain-of-custody requirements applicable in the Great Lakes region;
  • characterise tailings for waste management planning and to assess any future retreatment potential; and
  • prepare an order-of-magnitude assessment of the capital and operating cost implications of the recommended flowsheet, sufficient to inform the Stage 1 Gate Review.

Deliverables

  • Sampling and QA/QC Protocol (for Trinity's review prior to sample collection);
  • Metallurgical Testwork Report, including recommended flowsheet, recovery and grade outcomes, and supporting data; and
  • Stage 1 Gate Review Memorandum with a clear recommendation (proceed to Stage 2 / proceed subject to conditions / do not proceed) and supporting rationale.

Gate Criteria

Trinity does not presently have an independently validated benchmark for recovery or concentrate grade at Rutongo Mines for the purposes of this Study, given the absence of prior independent testwork. Trinity's own published materials cite an operating concentrate grade in the order of 70% tin; this figure has not been independently verified for the purposes of this Study and should be reconciled, not simply adopted, by the Consultant. The Consultant shall propose, for Trinity's agreement during mobilisation, numerical gate criteria covering as a minimum: (i) minimum acceptable recovery at a saleable concentrate grade; (ii) capital and operating cost order-of-magnitude consistent with a viable production case; and (iii) absence of a fatal environmental, geotechnical, or permitting flag arising from the testwork or associated site investigation. These criteria, once agreed, will govern the go/no-go decision at the end of Stage 1. Trinity retains sole approval authority over this gate (Section 8).

Stage 2 — Full Scoping Study (Contingent on Stage 1 Gate)

Stage 2 shall commence only once Trinity has confirmed that Rutongo Mines has satisfied its Stage 1 gate criteria (or that an agreed mitigation permits progression), and shall address the following disciplines, each to be reported to Scoping Study-level accuracy and detail (see Annex B):

Geology and Mineral Resources

  • compile, audit, and reconcile all available historical exploration data, including the 2018 AMS study (to the extent it covers this Mine) and the Stage 0 data review, against current mine development and production records;
  • estimate and classify Mineral Resources (Inferred, and Indicated where data quality supports it) in accordance with the JORC Code (2012), under the supervision of, and signed off by, a Competent Person;
  • identify data gaps constraining resource confidence and recommend infill drilling or sampling required to support future Ore Reserve estimation at PFS level; this Study shall define the Mineral Resource and development potential only, and shall not purport to estimate Ore Reserves;
  • undertake a preliminary evaluation of historical tailings, dumps, rejects, and alluvial, eluvial, and colluvial gravels within the licence area as a potential secondary source of feed, and determine whether further sampling or resource definition of these materials is warranted; and
  • document geological and structural controls on mineralisation relevant to mine planning.
  • estimate and classify Mineral Resources separately for each of the six historical areas (Gisanze, Masoro, Nyamyumba, Gasambya, Karambo, and Mahaza) before compiling a single, consolidated Rutongo Mineral Resource statement; and
  • given the scale of historical operations at Rutongo, place particular emphasis on evaluating alluvial, eluvial, and colluvial gravels and historical dumps across the six areas as a potential near-term or supplementary feed source.

Mining

  • assess the pathway from current mine development to a fully formalised, mechanised mine plan, including mining method selection suited to the steeply west-dipping, north–south trending quartz-vein mineralisation style (typical vein widths of 0.5–1 m) on the Rutongo anticline;
  • assess the condition of existing underground workings and surface access (declines, shafts, haul roads), building on the Stage 0 inspection, and confirm the extent to which existing development can be reused;
  • characterise geotechnical conditions (rock mass quality, ground support requirements) and hydrogeological conditions (groundwater inflow and dewatering requirements) at a scoping level;
  • assess ventilation requirements, including upgrade options for any existing ventilation infrastructure, and assess requirements for mine services (compressed air, underground power reticulation, communications, materials handling) and dewatering systems;
  • prepare a conceptual mine design and production schedule (development, stoping/extraction sequence, and ramp-up) consistent with the classified Mineral Resource; and
  • outline a workforce transition plan describing how existing artisanal or semi-artisanal labour may be absorbed into, or otherwise affected by, a fully formalised operation.
  • assess each of the six areas individually — including the existing Nyamyumba and Karambo plants and their current condition, capacity, and suitability for continued or expanded use — before consolidating into a single, sequenced Rutongo development case that addresses shared infrastructure, common services, and area-to-area ore and material scheduling.

Infrastructure

  • assess power supply options (grid connection versus diesel/hybrid generation) and overall water management, including raw/process water supply, mine dewatering discharge, and stormwater management;
  • assess access road and logistics requirements between the mine, processing facility, and export routes;
  • assess the condition, remaining capacity, and (where applicable) expansion, upgrade, or closure requirements of any existing tailings storage facilities, and site any new or expanded TSF capacity required, incorporating lessons learned from Trinity's Nyakabingo TSF trade-off study;
  • identify and site, at a conceptual level, the processing plant and any camp/accommodation requirements, incorporating lessons learned from Trinity's Nyakabingo plant design where relevant; and
  • identify shared infrastructure opportunities or constraints relative to the other Mine and to Trinity's other Rwandan operations, where relevant.

Environmental and Social

  • establish the existing environmental and social baseline (drawing on any legacy studies made available and the Consultant's own site-based investigation, including work carried out in Stage 0) and undertake a gap analysis against the requirements for a formal operation;
  • address artisanal/semi-artisanal miner formalisation, livelihood, and (if applicable) resettlement considerations arising from the transition to mechanised mining;
  • scope the requirements for a full Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) at the next study stage; and
  • provide an order-of-magnitude closure cost estimate.

Market and Marketing

  • review Trinity’s marketing report outlining the market for tin (cassiterite) concentrate, including indicative pricing, payability terms, and offtake structures; and
  • confirm product specification and chain-of-custody/conflict-free certification requirements (e.g. ITSCI) applicable to concentrate sales from the Great Lakes region.

Capital and Operating Cost Estimates

  • prepare capital cost estimates to a nominal ±25–35% accuracy, using a factored or analogous estimating basis appropriate to Scoping Study level, with an allowance for undefined items of up to 30%; and
  • prepare operating cost estimates to the same accuracy standard, covering mining, processing, site services, and site general and administration costs.

Financial Model and Risk

  • prepare a preliminary cash flow model and indicative economic outcomes (e.g. NPV and IRR) with sensitivity analysis on price, head grade, and metallurgical recovery, noting that a fully worked discounted cash flow is not required at Scoping Study level but a preliminary assessment is expected;
  • prepare a risk register identifying the principal technical, commercial, environmental, social, and permitting risks and opportunities specific to this Mine; and
  • prepare an indicative development schedule (bar-chart level) from study completion through to first fully mechanised production.
  • present indicative economics both on an area-by-area basis (for each of the six historical areas) and as a single consolidated Rutongo development case, clearly showing the basis of consolidation.

Recommendation

Provide a clear, independently supported recommendation for Rutongo Mines, for Trinity's approval: proceed to Pre-Feasibility Study; undertake further targeted testwork, drilling, or investigation before a PFS decision; or do not proceed — together with the supporting rationale and, where applicable, the estimated cost and duration of the recommended next step.

Eligibility and Competency Requirements

Interested parties must have

  • A company profile and statement of relevant experience, with particular reference to: tin/tantalum (3T) or comparable pegmatite-hosted mineral projects; scoping, pre-feasibility, or feasibility studies supporting the transition of artisanal or semi-artisanal operations to mechanized mining; and prior work in the Great Lakes region of Central/East Africa, including familiarity with conflict-free mineral chain-of-custody schemes (e.g. ITSCI).
  • A proposed methodology and work plan, explicitly addressing the three-stage, gated structure described in Section 3.2.
  • Curricula vitae of proposed key personnel, at minimum: Study/Project Manager; Resource Geologist (Competent Person under JORC); Mining Engineer; Metallurgist/Process Engineer; Environmental and Social Specialist; and Cost Estimator.
  • Details of relevant projects completed or underway in the last three to five years of a similar nature, scale, or geography, including client references who may be contacted.
  • Evidence of financial standing, such as summary financial statements or auditor's reports for the past three years.
  • A comprehensive health and safety record for the preceding three years.
  • Disclosure of any litigation or arbitration, current or within the last five years, in which the Invitee has been involved, including parties, subject matter, and amounts in dispute.
  • An indicative fee proposal for Stage 0, Stage 1, and Stage 2, including a rate card by personnel category, estimated hours/duration, disbursements, and key assumptions (see Annex C).
  • A description of the Invitee's proposed approach to engaging Rwandan sub-consultants, laboratories, and personnel, and to knowledge transfer — this will be assessed favourably as a qualification factor but is not a mandatory requirement.
  • A conflict-of-interest declaration, including disclosure of any existing relationship with Trinity, its shareholders, or competing projects in the licence area.

All interested parties should submit an Expression of Interest in accordance with the below requirements complete with supporting documents.

Submission to be forwarded to tender@trinity-metals.com  by not later than 14th September 2026 at 11:00 AM Local time. Expressions of Interest received after 14th September 2026 at 11:00 AM Local time will unfortunately not be considered.

Further discussion will be undertaken with selected respondents to prove the competence of the bidder and thereafter an invitation to tender will be provided to the bidder.

5. Location of supermarkets

Interested supermarkets must be located within 10 km of DUHAMIC-ADRI's head office in Kicukiro, Niboye sector.

6. Submission Requirements:

Interested bidders shall submit the following documents:

  • Financial quotation inclusive of all applicable taxes and transportation/delivery costs from the supermarket to DUHAMIC-ADRI Head Office
  • Company registration certificate issued by RDB
  • Proof of using EBM
  • Valid tax clearance certificate issued by RRA

Note:

  1. The supermarket must be physically established and stocked with the required items, as DUHAMIC-ADRI will conduct a visit before awarding the tender.
  2. The sample shall be available for review by bidders from September 1 to September 3, 2026 extended until September 10,2026 during working hours.

7. Submission Deadline

Bids must be submitted no later than September 04, 2026 at 02:00 PM extended until 11 September 2026 at 02:00 PM local Kigali time. Late submissions will be rejected without review (Only hard copies shall be accepted)

8. Bid Opening

Bids will be opened publicly on September 04, 2026 at 02:30 PM extended until 11 September 2026 at 02:30 PM at DUHAMIC-ADRI head office located in Kicukiro District, Niboye sector. Bidders or their authorized representatives are invited to attend.

9. Delivery Terms and Conditions

The following delivery conditions shall apply throughout the contract period:

  • Delivery shall be made to the DUHAMIC-ADRI Head Office located in Kicukiro District, Niboye Sector.
  • Quoted unit prices must be inclusive of all transportation and delivery costs to the above-mentioned delivery point.
  • Purchase Orders (POs) shall be issued by DUHAMIC-ADRI on a needs-basis. The supplier is therefore expected to maintain sufficient stock to respond to orders.
  • Delivery shall be made within the timeframe specified on each individual Purchase Order. Failure to deliver within the stipulated timeframe may result in penalties as outlined in the contract.
  • All products supplied must be in good condition, within their validity/expiry period, and properly packaged.

10. Pricing and Payment

  • Suppliers shall quote unit prices inclusive of tax and delivery cost to DUHAMIC-ADRI Head Office, Kicukiro District, Niboye Sector.
  • Payment shall be processed upon delivery and upon submission of invoice(s), supported by delivery notes signed by authorized DUHAMIC-ADRI personnel.

11. Duration of contract

The successful bidder will enter into a one-year (with possibility of renewal basing on the performance) contract with DUHAMIC-ADRI

12. Safeguarding clause

Safeguarding and protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) is everyone’s responsibility who works directly or indirectly with DUHAMIC-ADRI services delivery and operations. All DUHAMIC-ADRI staff and affiliates, including volunteers and Suppliers; sub-Suppliers’ staff and implementing partners are required to adhere to DUHAMIC-ADRI’s full safeguarding and protection policy procedures and the separate Code of Conduct that always values principles of PSEA.

DUHAMIC-ADRI has a zero tolerance to Sexual Exploitation and any other form of abuse. Child and vulnerable abuse, exploitation, harassment, discrimination, and human trafficking are strongly prohibited behaviours. All implementing partners/suppliers who are contracting with DUHAMIC-ADRI must adhere to DUHAMIC-ADRI’s full safeguarding and protection policy in addition to the code of conduct.

By applying to this tender, the supplier, is committed to denounce and to report any safeguarding issues or fraud face to face or at the reporting email for safeguarding issues at” feedback@duhamic.org.rw ”, Toll Free: 8470 and telephone number: 0788305329 without delays.

By Applying to this tender as a supplier, I understand that DUHAMIC-ADRI has the rights to ensure 100% compliance with safeguarding and protection policies via spot checks or any other form of control mechanisms. If my business isn’t compliant, DUHAMIC-ADRI will take appropriate measures or immediately stop the contract of financial support depending on the nature and severity of the safeguarding incident detected.

13. Data Protection and confidentiality

The successful bidder shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws in force in the Republic of Rwanda, including Law No. 058/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy. Any personal data, confidential information, or organizational records accessed during contract execution shall be used solely for the purposes of performing the contract, kept strictly confidential, and protected against unauthorized access, disclosure, loss, or misuse. Such data shall not be shared with third parties without prior written authorization from DUHAMIC-ADRI, and any actual or suspected data breach shall be reported immediately.

Note:

  • The quoted unit prices will remain fixed for the entire contract period
  • Prior to contracting, DUHAMIC-ADRI reserves the right to conduct a vetting process to the successful bidders to ensure compliance with anti-terrorism and other regulatory requirements.
  • DUHAMIC-ADRI reserves the right to conduct due diligence on all documents submitted by the bidder. If any reference is found to be unauthentic, the bidder shall be immediately disqualified.
  • Bidders who are blacklisted by RPPA are not eligible to participate in this tender. DUHAMIC-ADRI reserves the right to reject such bids.
  • Women-, youth-, and persons-with-disabilities–led companies that meet the required conditions and qualifications are encouraged to apply.
