greatrwandajobs.title: Irrigation Instructor job at Rwanda Rural Rehabilitation Initiative
greatrwandajobs.location: Amizero Institute of Technology and Hospitality (AMITH), Kayonza District
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background

Rwanda Rural Rehabilitation Initiative (RWARRI) is a non-governmental organization dedicated to promoting and improving the socio-economic welfare of rural communities in Rwanda. The organization was conceived in 1994 and started implementing its activities in Rwanda in 1995. RWARRI is registered with the Rwanda Governance Board (RGB), a government body tasked with regulating Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), under registration number 023/11. For promoting education, RWARRI initiated a technical and vocational education training (TVET) school named Amizero Institute of Technology and Hospitality (AMITH). This school started operating with the trades of Culinary Art, Hairdressing, Masonry, Tailoring, Welding, and Carpentry.

With the idea of expanding its contribution to the development of rural areas through agriculture and youth employment, RWARRI is partnering with SUYANA Foundation, a Switzerland-based organization whose aim is to support individuals and communities by enhancing health, education, and livelihood, and fostering local commitment for long-lasting positive impact. This partnership is initiating short courses in agriculture in the trades of Mechanization, Irrigation, and Post-Harvest Handling and Storage, through a project named Shaping the Next Generation of Agriculture, or Youth Empowerment for Sustainable and Profitable Agriculture in Rwanda (YESPAR).

In line with the Rwanda TVET Board (RTB) Training Organization Guide (TOG) for Short Courses in Irrigation Technology, RWARRI is recruiting an Irrigation Instructor and an Irrigation Teaching Assistant to jointly ensure effective delivery of theoretical and practical irrigation training at AMITH TVET School. This document presents the Terms of Reference (ToR) for both positions.

Positions Covered by this ToR

Two complementary positions are being recruited under the YESPAR project at AMITH. A brief overview of each is given below — full duties, responsibilities, and expected outputs are detailed in the respective full Terms of Reference.

Position 1: Irrigation Instructor — leads theoretical and practical training delivery (8 months).

Position 2: Irrigation Teaching Assistant — supports the Irrigation Instructor in lesson delivery and workshop management (6 months).

POSITION 1 — IRRIGATION INSTRUCTOR

Position Title: Irrigation Instructor

Duty Station: Amizero Institute of Technology and Hospitality (AMITH), Kayonza District

Reports To: AMITH School Manager and YESPAR Project Manager (RWARRI)

Duration: Eight (8) months, renewable or not

Project: Youth Empowerment for Sustainable and Profitable Agriculture in Rwanda (YESPAR)

Purpose of the Role

The Irrigation Instructor will be responsible for training YESPAR-supported students in irrigation technology, ensuring they acquire both the theoretical knowledge and practical skills necessary for employment or entrepreneurship as drip irrigation system operators, overhead (sprinkler) irrigation system operators, surface irrigation system operators, and irrigation pumping system operators, while respecting safety, security, and environmental regulations.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Irrigation and Drainage, Water Engineering, or a related field, with at least 1 year of relevant experience. Strong practical skills in irrigation systems and pumping equipment, plus good communication and mentoring ability.

greatrwandajobs.title: Territory Lead job at EarthEnable Rwanda
greatrwandajobs.description:
Who We Are

At EarthEnable, we believe that our clients deserve our very best, that work should be fun, and that the best ideas could come from any part of the company. We celebrate each other’s wins, learn from our setbacks, and are deeply proud of the impact we make every day. We believe a home that doesn’t make you sick means more than living disease-free. It means pride and dignity in the place our customers most treasure: their homes. Being a part of our team means more than building housing products: it means building an organization and building a better future for rural families.

What We Do

EarthEnable is transforming the way people live, by making homes healthier for families across rural Rwanda, Uganda, and Kenya. 80% of Rwandans live in homes with dirt floors which are dusty, unsanitary, and fertile breeding grounds for parasites and germs. While replacing a dirt floor with concrete has significant health benefits (e.g. reducing diarrhea by 50% and parasitic infections by 80%), concrete is unaffordable for many who need it, and is also responsible for 8% of global carbon emissions.

EarthEnable addresses this pressing and ubiquitous problem by selling high-quality, earthen housing products like our flagship floor that is 80% cheaper than concrete with 90% less embedded energy. Earthen floors, plasters, and blocks are composed of natural materials (gravel, clay, sand, and laterite) and sealed with a proprietary drying oil that makes them waterproof, strong, and polished. In our first decade of operations, EarthEnable has installed ~60,000 products for over 300,000 individuals and created livelihoods for over 1,300 people. See our new product - a full house - here!

Position Overview

The Territory Lead is responsible for the overall performance, growth, and operational excellence of their assigned territory. This role combines commercial leadership, operational oversight, and people management to ensure sales targets are met, construction projects are executed efficiently, and customers receive an exceptional experience.

The ideal candidate is a proactive and results-driven leader who can translate strategy into execution, build high-performing teams, and operate with strong business acumen in dynamic field environments.

Key Responsibilities

1. Territory Ownership and Business Performance

  • Own the end-to-end performance of the territory, ensuring alignment with company growth objectives and operational priorities.
  • Develop and execute localized sales and operational strategies informed by market insights, customer needs, and competitive dynamics.
  • Drive achievement of assigned sales and build targets while maintaining strong quality and customer satisfaction standards.
  • Monitor territory performance through data and KPIs, proactively identifying risks and implementing corrective actions.

2. Sales Leadership and Customer Experience

  • Lead the recruitment, onboarding, training, and ongoing development of Customer Sales Officers (CSOs) to build a strong and productive sales force.
  • Equip teams with the tools, messaging, and support needed to effectively engage customers and convert leads.
  • Champion customer-centric practices, ensuring a seamless journey from initial engagement through project completion.
  • Strengthen relationships with cooperatives, institutions, local leaders, and community stakeholders to expand market reach and reinforce EarthEnable’s mission.
  • Oversee territory-level marketing and activation initiatives to drive demand and brand visibility.

3. Operational and Construction Excellence

  • Oversee all construction activities within the territory, ensuring adherence to quality standards, timelines, and safety practices.
  • Align construction capacity with sales volume to prevent project delays and backlog.
  • Partner closely with operations teams to coordinate material forecasting, ordering, and delivery.
  • Track project progress and ensure timely follow-up on active builds, addressing bottlenecks before they escalate.
  • Continuously identify opportunities to improve construction efficiency and reduce cycle times.

4. Financial Stewardship and Data Integrity

  • Ensure customer payments are collected in accordance with company policies while maintaining the highest standards of financial accountability.
  • Monitor territory-level financial indicators, including revenue, cost drivers, and operational efficiency.
  • Promote accurate and timely data capture to support reporting, forecasting, and informed decision-making.
  • Safeguard company resources by reinforcing compliance with internal controls.

5. Team Leadership and Culture Building

  • Build, lead, and retain a high-performing territory team across sales and construction functions.
  • Provide regular coaching, mentorship, and structured performance feedback to strengthen capability and accountability.
  • Foster a culture grounded in professionalism, collaboration, continuous learning, and results.
  • Model EarthEnable’s values and cultivate an environment where team members feel motivated, supported, and empowered to succeed.

Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Sales, Operations, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 3+ years of progressive experience in field operations, sales leadership, or territory management.
  • Demonstrated success managing teams and delivering measurable business results.
  • Strong operational mindset with the ability to balance commercial growth and execution quality.
  • Experience working in fast-paced or growth-oriented organizations is highly desirable.
  • Proficiency in data-driven decision-making and performance management.

Key Competencies

  • Strong leadership and people development skills
  • Results-oriented with high ownership and accountability
  • Strategic thinker with strong execution capability
  • Excellent stakeholder and community engagement skills
  • Financial and operational discipline
  • Adaptability and resilience in dynamic environments
  • Clear communicator with the ability to influence and motivate teams

greatrwandajobs.description:

Job Brief:

The Shift Lubrication Technician is responsible for carrying out planned lubrication, inspection and basic condition-monitoring activities on equipment within the gravity tungsten recovery plant. The role ensures that bearings, gearboxes, pumps, conveyors, crushers, screens, gravity recovery equipment and other lubricated components receive the correct lubricant, in the correct quantity and at the required frequency. The technician also identifies and reports early signs of equipment deterioration, contamination, leakage, overheating, abnormal noise or vibration to support reliable plant operation, reduce unplanned downtime and improve equipment availability.

Responsibilities or duties

  • Ensure lubrication equipment, grease guns, pumps, hoses and related tools are clean, serviceable and correctly identified.
  • Inspect lubrication points and associated equipment for leaks, damaged seals, contamination, overheating, abnormal noise, vibration and other indications of developing equipment failure.
  • Lubricate bearings, gearboxes, chains, couplings, pumps, conveyor components and other designated lubrication points using the correct lubricant, quantity and application method.
  • Carry out scheduled lubrication routes and lubrication tasks in accordance with approved maintenance plans, manufacturer recommendations and Company procedures.
  • Use only approved oils, greases and other lubricants specified for each item of plant equipment.
  • Prevent cross-contamination by using dedicated, clean and correctly labelled lubrication equipment and containers.
  • Maintain lubricant storage and handling practices to protect lubricants from water, dust, dirt and other contaminants.
  • Report incorrect, contaminated, expired or insufficient lubricant stock to the supervisor responsible.
  • Escalate critical defects immediately where continued operation could result in equipment damage, safety risk or production loss.
  • Assist with oil sampling and basic lubricant condition checks where required and ensure samples are correctly identified and submitted.
  • Report abnormal temperature, noise, vibration, oil condition, grease condition, leakage, seal failure or other defects requiring mechanical attention.
  • Monitor equipment condition while performing lubrication activities and identify early signs of mechanical deterioration.
  • Assist maintenance personnel during planned maintenance activities where lubrication expertise is required.
  • Contribute to the prevention of premature bearing, gearbox, pump and other component failures through disciplined lubrication practices.
  • Assist with lubrication route optimization, equipment criticality reviews and improvements to lubrication frequencies and practices where required.
  • Support the Engineering team in preventive maintenance activities related to lubrication and equipment reliability.
  • Work closely with plant operators and maintenance personnel to identify equipment problems and ensure timely intervention.
  • Coordinate lubrication activities with plant operations to minimise disruption to production while maintaining safe working conditions.
  • Complete shift handovers and communicate outstanding lubrication tasks, defects and equipment concerns to the incoming team.
  • Respond to lubrication-related breakdown or urgent maintenance requirements when called upon.
  • Accurately record all completed lubrication activities, inspections, lubricant usage, defects and corrective actions in the applicable maintenance records or system.
  • Maintain accurate lubrication route checklists and report missed or inaccessible lubrication points.
  • Report recurring equipment and lubrication problems to the Mechanical / Maintenance Shift Supervisor.
  • Support the development and updating of lubrication schedules, lubrication point registers and relevant maintenance procedures.
  • Ensure all work is performed in compliance with Company health and safety standards, environmental requirements, risk assessments and safe work procedures.
  • Apply isolation and lock-out/tag-out requirements before working on equipment where required.
  • Use the correct PPE and safe handling practices when working with oils, greases, cleaning agents and other maintenance materials.
  • Prevent and immediately report oil and grease spills, leaks and environmental contamination, and maintain good housekeeping in work areas.
  • Participate in safety meetings, toolbox talks, inspections and risk assessments.
  • Participate in relevant technical training and maintain competency in lubrication practices and equipment reliability.
  • Share lubrication-related observations and practical knowledge with operators, fitters and other maintenance personnel.
  • Identify opportunities to improve lubrication practices, equipment reliability, housekeeping and maintenance efficiency.
  • Assist with implementing approved improvements to lubrication systems, equipment and procedures.
  • Comply with Company work and leave schedules.
  • Comply with all Company policies, procedures and instructions.
  • Perform other duties as required by the Superior or Management, within the scope of the role.

Qualifications or requirements 

  • A minimum of a Technical and Vocational Education Training (TVET) Certificate III in Mechanical Fitting, Lubrication, Maintenance or a related field.
  • Training or certification in industrial lubrication, condition monitoring or equipment maintenance is advantageous.
  • Good knowledge of industrial lubricants, grease and oil application methods, lubrication frequencies and contamination control.
  • Ability to identify common signs of equipment deterioration, including abnormal heat, noise, vibration, leakage and lubricant degradation.
  • Ability to use lubrication tools, grease guns, oil transfer equipment and basic inspection equipment correctly.
  • Ability to read and understand lubrication schedules, equipment manuals, maintenance instructions and basic technical drawings.
  • Basic understanding of mechanical equipment and the relationship between correct lubrication and equipment reliability.
  • Excellent attention to detail, organization and time-management skills.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills, with commitment to safety and compliance.
  • Ability to use and work with English as the business language.
  • Ability to work independently and follow planned lubrication routes and schedules accurately.
  • Strong problem-identification and reporting skills.
  • Physically fit to work in challenging plant and mining conditions, including standing, walking, climbing, bending and working around operating industrial equipment.
  • Able to handle lubrication equipment and lubricant containers safely and work in areas that may be wet, dusty, noisy or confined.
  • Willingness to work shifts, overtime and respond to urgent maintenance requirements as required.
  • Commitment to ongoing professional development and staying updated with lubrication, maintenance and equipment reliability practices.

Experience needed

At least 2 years of experience in industrial maintenance, lubrication or a similar engineering role, preferably in a mining or mineral processing environment.

Practical experience working with rotating plant equipment, bearings, gearboxes, pumps, conveyors and related mechanical equipment.

Trinity Metals Ltd is seeking for a qualified and local Rwandan service provider to provide Professional Architectural Design, BoQ and Building permit support for Trinity Nyakabingo Administration Block.

SCOPE OF WORK

Professional Architectural Design, BoQ and Building Permit Support – Nyakabingo Administration Block

Trinity Nyakabingo Mine Ltd. intends to engage a qualified and professionally registered architectural consultant to design the proposed Nyakabingo Administration Block from scratch.

The previously prepared architectural drawings provided by the Client shall be used for reference only, particularly for understanding the general intended spaces and functional requirements. The Consultant shall not be limited to or required to reproduce the existing design.

The selected Consultant shall provide the following services:

1. Architectural Design

  • Develop a complete architectural design for the proposed Administration Block based on the Client's requirements.
  • Prepare all necessary architectural drawings, including floor plans, elevations, sections, roof plan and relevant details.
  • Present the design to the Client and incorporate reasonable comments until internal approval is obtained.

2. Bill of Quantities

  • Prepare a detailed Bill of Quantities (BoQ) based on the approved design.
  • Provide an indicative construction cost estimate.

3. Professional Certification

  • Provide professionally signed, stamped and certified architectural drawings and other relevant documents required for the project and permit application (EIA Certification report).

4. Building Permit Support

  • Assist the Client with preparation and submission of the required documents for building permit application.
  • Provide the necessary certified professional documents required by the relevant Government authorities.

5. Amendments and Re-certification

  • Address comments or amendments raised by relevant Government authorities concerning the Consultant's design.
  • Revise and resubmit the affected drawings/documents where required.
  • Re-certify and stamp amended documents as necessary.

6. Final Deliverables

  • Final approved architectural design drawings.
  • Bill of Quantities.
  • Certified permit application documents.
  • Editable and PDF versions of the final design documents.

Important: The Consultant shall be responsible for correcting, amending and re-certifying any errors, omissions or design issues identified during the Client's review or by relevant Government authorities, at no additional professional fee.

Eligibility and Competency Requirements

Interested parties must:

  • Have a minimum of 5 years of demonstrated experience in Architectural Design, BoQ and Building Permit Support.
  • Possess a solid track record of working on similar projects and should be provided as part of submissions.
  • Where applicable, be registered with, or eligible to carry out similar services with, a recognized professional organization. 
  • Possess multidisciplinary engineering expertise and project management capabilities.

All interested parties should submit an Expression of Interest in accordance with the below requirements complete with supporting documents.

  • Application Cover Letter introducing your Company/Individual expressing interest, availability, and a brief business and experience profile including qualifications and experience.

greatrwandajobs.title: Advocacy and Policy Analyst job at Pro-Femmes/Twese Hamwe (PFTH)
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background

Pro-Femmes/ Twese Hamwe (PFTH) is an Umbrella of Rwandan Civil Society Organizations aiming at advancement of women status, peace and development. PFTH was established in October 1992 and currently represents 52 member organizations within the country. The mission of PFTH is to eradicate all forms of discrimination towards women, to promote their socio-economic, political and legal status, and to enhance the institutional and organizational capacities of its member organizations through the promotion of sustainable human development approach based on gender equality and a culture of peace, justice and human rights.

PFTH in partnership with CARE International in Rwanda is implementing a five years (2023-2027) project named the “Supporting and Enhancing Resilient and Viable Employment Opportunities (SERVE)”. The project aims to build a resilient, sustainable, and inclusive entrepreneurial environment that increases work opportunities in agricultural value chains in 10 districts namely Rulindo & Gakenke in Northern Province, Kayonza, Rwamagana, Ngoma & Kirehe in Eastern Province, Nyamagabe & Huye in Southern Province and Nyabihu & Rubavu in Western Province. Under this partnership, PFTH will collaborate with women and youth, women and youth groups, policy and market actors to address the specific range of challenges women and youth face in participating in the policy and business environments. These include exclusion from policy discussions and decision-making and unequal power dynamics in markets that prevent them from accessing higher value nodes and that limit assist and investment in women and youth-led enterprise.

To contribute to the above said goal, PFTH is expected to make sure that:

  • The agricultural Medium and Small Enterprises (MSEs) policy and social norms environment is responsive, inclusive, and informed;
  • Women and youth have greater social capital and agency in engaging in agriculture;
  • Women and youth MSEs influence decision-making related to the agricultural value chain and public authorities are responsive and accountable to the needs and rights of women and youth-led MSEs.

Duty station: The Advocacy and policy analyst will be based at the PFTH Head Quarters with frequent travel to the above said 10 districts.

PFTH is therefore looking for a suitable candidate to fill the position of Advocacy Policy Analyst to guide the project advocacy initiative. Under the direct supervision of the project coordinator, the Advocacy Policy Analyst will undertake the following specific tasks:

Coordinating and facilitating the advocacy Process

To create suitable advocacy strategies and make sure that there are changes in policy, plans and actions that will contribute to sustainable improvements of the working environment of Project beneficiaries through engagement of policy makers and stakeholders to create enabling policy and legal frameworks.

Main tasks:

  • Along with PFTH management, create and execute PFTH advocacy strategy that is informed by PFTH members and project’s work on the ground;
  • track and take appropriate action on new and ongoing developments of policies, Laws, and program in line with priority and advocacy goals. This involves developing a clear understanding of the principal decision-making processes in Rwanda that are relevant to Pro- Femmes advocacy work;
  • Organize outreach events and engage with different stakeholders at grass root and national level, to build strong relationships with citizens/grassroots structures and government to inform PFTH Advocacy strategy;
  • Analyse current and emerging policy to propose policy alternatives in accordance with PFTH advocacy goals;
  • Organize and create opportunities/events (such as seminars, meetings) to enable PFTH and partners contribute to public and policy debate on key advocacy issues;
  • Update PFTH policy advocacy work, contribute to PFTH policy development, publications, planning and strategy, and liaise with PFTH members working on policy, Advocacy, research and others;
  • Collaborate with Rwanda civil society platform, networks and other CSOs and contribute to PFTH advocacy agenda;
  • Liaise with PFTH members and help with capacity strengthening especially on advocacy and policy analysis;
  • In collaboration with the Advocacy and Communication coordinator at PFTH engage with media, create communications materials and deliver opportunities for the public to learn more about PFTH work.

Sub Tasks:

  • Keeping updated with standards of professionalism and PFTH’s expectations concerning personal behaviour and values, and acting accordingly;
  • Participating in other events (e.g. national events) and networking opportunities.
  • Perform any duty assigned by the supervision;

DESIRED COMPETENCIES AND QUALIFICATIONS FOR COORDINATOR

  • Bachelor’s Development studies, Agriculture, Law, Public Administration, Business Administration, Management, Social sciences or any other related field;
  • Holders of master’s degree in relevant field are preferable for the prospective candidate;
  • At least four (3) years progressive experience in managing projects related to agriculture value chain, advocacy, gender-based violence and gender mainstreaming;
  • Strong understanding of the agricultural value chain;
  • Strong experience and knowledge of civil society in Rwanda;
  • Experience and knowledge of national and regional issues relevant to agriculture and trade
  • Experience in Networking, building coalitions, lobbying and advocacy especially for gender related issues;
  • Understanding of Human rights-based approach;
  • Fluency in English, French and Kinyarwanda.
  • Computer literate (high proficiency in words, Excel and Power point).
  • Excellent communicator orally and in writing;
  • Innovative, self –driven and team player;
  • Interpersonal skills with experience of working in multicultural contexts.

greatrwandajobs.title: Direct sales Agent (DSA) job at Letshego Rwanda Limited
greatrwandajobs.description:
About Letshego Rwanda Limited

Letshego Rwanda Limited (Letshego Rwanda) was established in Rwanda in 2004 and is a subsidiary of Letshego Holdings Limited (LHL), a pan African financial services group that is headquartered in Gaborone. LHL is the largest indigenous BSE-quoted company with a current market capitalisation in excess of BWP 5 billion (US$ 500 million) that places it in the top 40 sub-Saharan Africa companies (excluding-South Africa). Since inception Letshego Rwanda has been operating as a regulated credit only microfinance company. In 2013, Letshego Rwanda obtained a deposit-taking microfinance licence from the National Bank of Rwanda.

About This Opportunity

The position of Direct sales Agent (DSA) at Letshego Rwanda Limited located in Rusizi, Rwanda offers an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience in a dynamic working environment. The organization seeks individuals who are motivated, reliable, and capable of performing their duties effectively while maintaining professional standards.

JOB ADVERT

Letshego Holdings Limited was incorporated in 1998; it’s headquartered in Gaborone and has been publicly listed on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) since 2002. It is an inclusive finance focused group with consumer, micro-lending and deposit-taking subsidiaries across sub-Saharan Africa.

An opening has arisen within Letshego Rwanda Limited LRL for the below-mentioned position. This role is tenable at LRL.

POSITION: Direct sales Agent (DSA)

Reports to: The incumbent will report to Branch Manager.

Purpose of the Job:

The Direct sales Agent(DSA) plays a vital role in customer acquisition, credit assessment, portfolio growth, and client relationship management. The DSA is tasked with identifying potential clients, evaluating their creditworthiness, disbursing microloans, and ensuring timely repayments. This role requires a proactive, target-driven individual with strong interpersonal skills and a passion for financial inclusion and community development.

Key Accountabilities:

Client Acquisition & Onboarding

Detect and recruit new clients through field visits, referrals, and community engagement.

Perform orientation and financial literacy sessions for new clients.

Assist clients in completing loan applications and ensuring all required documents are submitted.

Loan Assessment & Disbursement

Carry out detailed credit assessments, including household visits and business evaluations.

Produce loan proposals and present them to the Branch Credit Committee.

Facilitate timely loan disbursements while ensuring adherence to credit policies and procedures.

Portfolio Management

Track loan utilization and deliver assist to clients to ensure productive use of funds.

Perform regular follow-ups to ensure on-time loan repayments.

Detect and address early warning signs of repayment challenges.

Customer Relationship Management

Keep strong relationships with clients by providing excellent after-loan service and assist.

Address client complaints or concerns professionally and escalate when necessary.

Promote other financial products such as savings, insurance, or mobile banking.

Reporting & Compliance

Keep accurate records of client interactions, loan files, and repayment schedules.

Submit daily, weekly, and monthly reports on loan performance and field activities.

Ensure full compliance with internal policies, credit guidelines, and regulatory requirements.

Qualifications and Experience:

Bachelor’s degree or diploma in any related field.

At least 1–2 years of experience in microfinance, sales, or customer service is preferred.

Basic understanding of credit assessment and micro-lending practices.

Strong communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.

Proficiency in MS Office and familiarity with mobile or digital banking tools.

Ability to ride a motorcycle (with a valid license) is often an added advantage for fieldwork

Embrace the Group uniquenesses

The job holder shall, at all times embrace Group uniqueness’s set out below:

Simple - Straight forward and uncomplicated

Appropriate - Relevant and suitable

Accessible - Welcoming and consistent

Ethical - Honest and principled

Responsive - Receptive and compassionate

Inclusive - Embracing and proactive

Deciding and Initiating Action

Leading and Supervising

Working with People

Adhering to principles & values

Relating and Networking

Persuading and Influencing

Presenting and Communicating Information

Writing and Reporting

Learning & Researching

Planning and Organizing

Coping with Pressures and Setbacks

Commercial Thinking

Analytical

Additional Information:

Jobholder should be a person of high integrity and discretion with confidential matters. Multi-cultural awareness and the ability to interact with a wide range of differing levels and sectors of staff, society, social and business, is an essential characteristic of the person holding this position.

greatrwandajobs.title: Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer job at Development Bank of Rwanda
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background Information

The Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD) Plc is Rwanda’s only National Development Bank mandated to assist Rwanda’s Vision 2050 development agenda. Over the past five years, the bank has registered exponential growth contributing to socio-economic development, strengthening institutional and human capacity, fostering corporate governance and risk management practices.

The Bank is implementing the revised strategic plan for 2026-2029 which is appropriately aligned to the country’s strategic direction enabling the Bank to unlock better value creation for its stakeholders by supporting entrepreneurs, addressing market failures, and impactful socioeconomic development.

To deliver on its bold vision and impactful objectives, the Bank’s expanded and refocused mandate is underpinned on four strategic focus areas:

  • Availing transformational finance.
  • Increasing green financing for a resilient future.
  • Driving scale and impact.
  • Fostering innovation and technology.

To achieve its strategic mandate, BRD recognizes the importance of strengthening its human and institutional capital to drive sustainable development and ensure the Bank remains a center of excellence in the financial sector.

BRD is committed to respecting gender equality and disability norms. We promote gender-responsive practices. Qualified candidates particularly females and persons living with disabilities are encouraged to apply.

To help accomplish this ambitious and exciting vision, the Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD) would like to recruit suitable qualified candidates to fill the following position:

Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer

Background Information

Job Title: Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer Job Grade: JG G-Specialist

Division: IT & Digital Innovation

Reports to: Head, IT Operations

Contract terms: Open ended contract

Purpose of the Job

The Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer is responsible for safeguarding the quality, reliability, and compliance of the Bank's in-house developed digital tools, which are owned by the Application Management unit and supported operationally by the Service Management unit within a hybrid (on-premises and cloud) IT environment. These tools support special projects and manage the end-to-end client journey, including client and account management, accounting, reporting, and operations & maintenance (O&M). The applications run on mixed architectures — some monolithic, others microservices-based — hosted across on-premises and cloud infrastructure, and are deployed by development teams through CI/CD pipelines. The QA Engineer designs and executes test strategies across this hybrid estate, embeds automated quality gates in the CI/CD process, and works closely with the Application Management and Service Management units, the IT Infrastructure unit, and the Database and Data Platform unit, to ensure that every release meets the Bank's functional, security, performance, and regulatory expectations before it reaches clients.

Main Responsibilities of the Job

Duties and responsibilities shall include but not limited to:

A. Test Strategy, Planning & Design

  • Define test strategies, test plans, and test cases for in-house applications covering client management, accounting, reporting, and O&M workflows.
  • Analyze business and technical requirements with developers, business analysts, and project teams to ensure testability and full requirement coverage.
  • Establish and maintain traceability between requirements, test cases, defects, and releases.

B. Functional, Regression & UAT Testing

  • Execute functional, regression, smoke, and end-to-end testing across monolithic and microservices-based applications deployed on-premises and in the cloud.
  • Validate financial accuracy of accounting and reporting modules, including reconciliations, postings, and report outputs.
  • Plan, coordinate, and support User Acceptance Testing (UAT) with business units, including preparation of UAT scripts, environments, data, and sign-off instruments.

C. Test Automation & CI/CD Quality Gates

  • Design, build, and maintain automated test suites (UI, API, and integration) using industry tools and frameworks.
  • Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines so that every build and deployment passes defined quality gates before promotion, in coordination with the Application Management unit.
  • Continuously expand regression automation coverage to reduce manual testing effort and release cycle time.

D. API, Integration & Microservices Testing

  • Test APIs, service contracts, and inter-service communication in the microservices estate (request/response validation, error handling, idempotency, and failure scenarios).
  • Validate integrations between in-house tools, core banking, payment channels, and external partners, whether hosted on-premises or in the cloud.
  • Verify data integrity and consistency across services, databases, and reporting layers, in coordination with the Database and Data Platform unit.

E. Non-Functional Testing

  • Conduct performance, load, and stress testing on customer-impacting services and batch/reporting processes across the hybrid infrastructure.
  • Support security-focused testing in collaboration with the Information Security team (input validation, access control, session management).
  • Test backup/restore, failover, and resilience behaviors where applicable, in coordination with the IT Infrastructure unit.

F. Defect Management & Quality Reporting

  • Log, prioritize, track, and verify defects through their lifecycle; drive root-cause analysis with developers and the Application Management unit.
  • Produce clear test summary reports, release readiness assessments, and quality dashboards for management and project governance.
  • Provide a documented go/no-go quality recommendation for each release, coordinated with the Service Management unit.

G. Quality Governance, Compliance & Continuous Improvement

  • Ensure testing practices comply with the Bank's change management, ISMS, and regulatory requirements, and support audit evidence requests.
  • Define and enforce quality standards, definitions of done, and entry/exit criteria for testing phases across on-premises and cloud releases.
  • Champion a quality culture within development and project teams, and continuously improve QA processes, tools, and test data management.

Performance Indicators

  • Defect leakage rate to production (post-release defects vs. defects caught in testing).
  • Test coverage of requirements and automation coverage of regression suites.
  • Release quality: percentage of releases passing quality gates without emergency fixes.
  • UAT cycle efficiency: timeliness of UAT preparation, execution, and sign-off.
  • Accuracy and completeness of test documentation, traceability, and quality reports.
  • Reduction in production incidents attributable to inadequate testing.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction from project and business teams.

Working relationships

Internal: Software Development, Application Management, Service Management, IT Infrastructure, Database and Data Platform, DevOps/DevSecOps, Information Security, Business Analysts, Special Project teams, Business units (Operations, Finance/Accounting, Reporting), Internal Audit.

External: Application vendors, integration partners, and third-party testing/tooling providers.

Professional, academic qualifications and experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or an equivalent field.
  • Minimum three (3) years of experience in software quality assurance/software testing, preferably in banking or financial services.
  • Hands-on experience with test automation tools and frameworks (e.g., Selenium, Playwright, Cypress) and API testing tools (e.g., Postman, REST Assured).
  • Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitLab CI, Jenkins, GitHub Actions).
  • Experience testing both monolithic and microservices/API-based applications across hybrid (on-premises and cloud) environments.
  • Strong SQL skills for test data preparation and back-end/data validation (Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, or similar).
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot and analyze complex defects originating from different integrated systems, tracing issues across front-end, APIs, services, databases, and external interfaces to pinpoint the failing component.
  • Experience with performance testing tools (e.g., JMeter, k6) is an advantage.
  • ISTQB certification (Foundation or higher) is an added advantage.

Core competencies

  • Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with a detail-oriented, risk-based approach to testing.
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex issues across multiple integrated systems and clearly attribute defects to the correct layer or component.
  • Solid understanding of banking workflows, financial data accuracy, and regulatory sensitivity.
  • Effective communication skills to report quality status clearly to technical and business stakeholders.
  • Structured documentation and traceability discipline.
  • Collaborative mindset with the ability to constructively challenge developers and project teams.
  • Ability to work under pressure, manage multiple parallel releases, and meet tight deadlines.
  • Continuous learning and adaptability to new tools, frameworks, and architectures.

Job Title: Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) Specialist. Job Grade: JG G- Specialist

Department: Strategy and Resource Mobilization.

Location: Kigali-Rwanda (BRD Head Office).

Reports to: Functionally to the Senior Manager, Strategy & Analytics Unit. Administratively to the Senior Project Coordinator for Export Credit Guarantee Facility (ECGF).

Contract terms: Open-Ended.

Purpose of the Job

BRD is recruiting for a Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Specialist in charge of conducting MEL activities for the Credit Guarantee function. The individual will lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of monitoring, evaluation, and learning results, tools, and frameworks. This role includes establishing tracking performance, collecting and analyzing data, ensuring timely and high-quality reporting on output/outcomes/impact, and ensuring adaptive learning to inform strategic decision-making and continuous improvement.

Main Responsibilities of the Job.

Monitoring.

  • Design and implement MEL systems for Credit guarantee department, including results chains, log frames, KPIs, and data collection tools, aligned with BRD’s MEL policy.
  • Oversee data collection, management, analysis and performance tracking from partner institutions and guarantee beneficiaries; generate monitoring reports for internal and external use.
  • Manage the MEL learning platform and integrate the credit guarantee impact tracking into BRD’s operational procedures.
  • Coordinate with stakeholders and consultants to support external evaluations and ensure stakeholder engagement.
  • Ensuring continuous Improvement using insights from data to refine strategies and improve overall projects effectiveness
  • Track and assess credit guarantee implementation progress to inform management and stakeholders on achievement of objectives, providing evidence-based recommendations for action.
  • Maintain and manage the Credit guarantee MEL database; analyze and aggregate data to generate timely insights.
  • Conduct regular field visits to beneficiaries and partners to verify data quality, support implementation, and identify areas for improvement.
  • Monitor implementation of evaluation recommendations in collaboration with the credit guarantee team.

Evaluation and Reporting.

  • Prepare regular detailed performance and seasonal/mid-impact assessments reports for all credit guarantee projects, including progress on KPIs and recommendations for action.
  • Conduct comparative analysis of project projections vs. actuals to inform strategic decision-making.
  • Conduct field surveys, midterm and final evaluations, and routine outcome assessments.
  • Identify performance issues and recommend improvements in systems, methodologies, or procedures.

Learning and Knowledge Management.

  • Facilitate learning reviews and reflection sessions to capture lessons learned, success stories, challenges and best practices to improve the credit guarantee implementation.
  • Document and disseminate case studies, success stories, and key lessons for wider stakeholder use.
  • Promote cross-learning within BRD and among fund partners to enhance knowledge sharing.
  • Develop and implement a learning agenda to strengthen adaptive management and continuous improvement.
  • Integrate learning outcomes into planning, decision-making, and performance reporting.
  • Collect and identify different project issues and set ways to address them

Compliance.

  • Produce quarterly and annual performance reports, ensure their approval, and share them to BRD management and development partners.
  • Ensure all MEL activities comply with BRD policies, donor requirements, and international best practices.
  • Support audits and evaluations by providing relevant documentation and MEL insights.

Capacity Building and Stakeholder Engagement.

  • Provide MEL training and technical support to partner institutions and MSMEs.
  • Build capacity of internal and external stakeholders on MEL tools and reporting requirements.
  • Engage with donors, consultants, and partners on MEL planning, execution, and learning activities.

Performance indicators

  • Quality and timeliness of MEL and projects’ performance reports produced.
  • Monthly progress reports produced & submitted to management describing major activities undertaken and tasks accomplished during the reporting period and challenges hindering implementation process.
  • Implemented Credit guarantee MEL Framework.
  • End of year project implementation performance report.
  • Quarterly stakeholder meeting minutes with stakeholders.
  • Field M&E reports, findings, and recommendations.
  • Compliance rate with credit agreements, internal policies, and applicable sector regulations.
  • Accuracy, reliability, and completeness of project data and information systems.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction levels with the credit guarantee performance.

Working relationships

All departments – especially SPI, Business Development, Credit Guarantee, Strategy and Resource Mobilization – and partner financial institutions, end-beneficiaries/clients.

Qualifications and Experience

Minimum Requirements.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Development Studies, Statistics, Business, or a related field.
  • At least 5 years of professional experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning and Research – preferably in financial services, MSME development, or development finance contexts.
  • Proven experience in designing and implementing MEL systems for complex projects or programs.
  • Strong knowledge of best practices in structured finance, blended finance, credit enhancement techniques, guarantees and international trade practices is desirable.

Desired Qualifications.

  • A postgraduate degree in Monitoring and Evaluation, Development Economics, or related fields is an asset.
  • Familiarity with credit guarantee facilities, or SME development programs.
  • Experience in using data analysis software (e.g., Excel, Power BI, STATA, or similar).
  • Strong report writing and stakeholder engagement skills.

Competencies.

  • Strong analytical and critical thinking skills.
  • Attention to detail and data accuracy.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams.
  • High standards of integrity and professionalism.

Job Title: Full Stack Software Engineer Job Grade: JG G- Specialist

Contract terms: Open ended contract

Purpose of the Job

The Full Stack Software Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, and delivering scalable, secure, and maintainable digital solutions using modern JavaScript frameworks — Next.js on the front end and Nest.js on the back end — with a strong command of microservices architecture. The role writes clean, high-standard code, crafts intuitive UI/UX, and actively applies AI to accelerate and elevate development work. greatrwandajobs.title: DevOps Engineer job at Development Bank of Rwanda
greatrwandajobs.description:
Background Information

The Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD) Plc is Rwanda’s only National Development Bank mandated to assist Rwanda’s Vision 2050 development agenda. Over the past five years, the bank has registered exponential growth contributing to socio-economic development, strengthening institutional and human capacity, fostering corporate governance and risk management practices.

The Bank is implementing the revised strategic plan for 2026-2029 which is appropriately aligned to the country’s strategic direction enabling the Bank to unlock better value creation for its stakeholders by supporting entrepreneurs, addressing market failures, and impactful socioeconomic development.

To deliver on its bold vision and impactful objectives, the Bank’s expanded and refocused mandate is underpinned on four strategic focus areas:

  • Availing transformational finance.
  • Increasing green financing for a resilient future.
  • Driving scale and impact.
  • Fostering innovation and technology.

To achieve its strategic mandate, BRD recognizes the importance of strengthening its human and institutional capital to drive sustainable development and ensure the Bank remains a center of excellence in the financial sector.

BRD is committed to respecting gender equality and disability norms. We promote gender-responsive practices. Qualified candidates particularly females and persons living with disabilities are encouraged to apply.

To help accomplish this ambitious and exciting vision, the Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD) would like to recruit suitable qualified candidates to fill the following position:

DevOps Engineer

Background Information

Job Title: DevOps Engineer Job Grade: JG G-Specialist

Division: IT & Digital Innovation – Digital Innovation Unit

Reports to: Head, Digital Innovation & Data

Contract terms: Open ended contract

Purpose of the Job

The DevOps Engineer is responsible for building and operating the platform that runs the Bank's microservices at scale. The role deploys and manages containerized microservices on Kubernetes, provisions and hardens clusters using open-source tooling such as Kubespray, and automates the full delivery lifecycle through CI/CD and Infrastructure as Code. The role brings a strong reliability and security mindset, a bias for automation, and genuine enthusiasm for the open-source ecosystem — continuously learning and adopting new tools, approaches, and methodologies as the landscape evolves.

Main Responsibilities of the Job

Duties and responsibilities shall include but not limited to:

  • Deploy microservices. Package, release, and operate containerized microservices on Kubernetes with zero-downtime strategies (rolling, blue-green, canary).
  • Provision Kubernetes clusters. Stand up, upgrade, and maintain production-grade clusters using open-source tooling such as Kubespray, including on-prem and bare-metal deployments.
  • Automate delivery (CI/CD). Design and maintain CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows for fast, safe, repeatable releases.
  • Manage infrastructure as code. Define and version infrastructure with tools like Terraform and Ansible; treat environments as reproducible code.
  • Ensure reliability & observability. Implement monitoring, logging, tracing, alerting, and SLOs; lead incident response and continuous improvement.
  • Harden security & compliance. Apply container and cluster security, secrets management, RBAC, and network policies aligned to best practice.
  • Optimize cost & performance. Right-size workloads, tune autoscaling, and improve resource efficiency across clusters.
  • Collaborate, mentor, and keep learning. Partner with developers, contribute to open-source where relevant, and continuously adopt new tools and methodologies.

Performance Indicators

  • Platform availability and uptime of Kubernetes clusters and hosted microservices.
  • Deployment frequency, lead time for changes, and change failure rate (DORA metrics).
  • Mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to recover (MTTR) for platform incidents.
  • Coverage of infrastructure managed as code and automation of previously manual tasks.
  • Security and compliance posture: RBAC, secrets management, image scanning, and policy adherence.
  • Cost and resource efficiency improvements across clusters and workloads.

Working relationships

Internal: Digital Innovation, Software Development, Application Management, Service Management, IT Infrastructure, Database and Data Platform, Information Security, Internal Audit.External: Cloud service providers, infrastructure and tooling vendors, integration partners, open-source communities.

Professional, academic qualifications and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.
  • Typically, two (2)+ years in DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering, including hands-on Kubernetes in production and cluster provisioning with tools such as Kubespray.
  • Certifications (CKA/CKAD/CKS, Terraform Associate) and open-source contributions are an advantage; fintech/banking experience is a plus.

Core competencies

Technical Skills — Containers & Orchestration

  • Strong hands-on experience deploying and operating microservices on Kubernetes in production.
  • Cluster provisioning and lifecycle management with open-source tooling such as Kubespray; Helm for packaging and Kustomize for configuration.
  • Docker and container best practices (image hardening, multi-stage builds, registries).

Technical Skills — CI/CD & Automation

  • CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins) and GitOps (Argo CD or Flux).
  • Scripting and automation (Bash, Python, or Go) to eliminate manual toil.

Technical Skills — Infrastructure as Code & Cloud

  • Infrastructure as Code with Terraform and configuration management with Ansible.
  • Experience with at least one cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) and/or on-prem and bare-metal environments; Linux administration and networking.

Technical Skills — Observability, Reliability & Security

  • Monitoring and logging stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK/Loki) and distributed tracing (Jaeger/OpenTelemetry).
  • Cluster and supply-chain security (RBAC, network policies, secrets management, image scanning); familiarity with service mesh (Istio/Linkerd) is a plus.

Core Competencies & Mindset

  • Fast learner. Quickly ingests and applies new tools, open-source projects, approaches, and methodologies with minimal ramp-up.
  • Automation-first & systems thinking. Automates by default and reasons about the whole distributed system, not just single components.
  • Reliability & ownership. Takes end-to-end accountability for uptime, performance, and security, with strong attention to detail.
  • Open-source oriented. Comfortable reading, adopting, and contributing to open-source tooling like Kubespray and the broader CNCF ecosystem.
  • Collaboration & communication. Works effectively with developers and stakeholders and communicates clearly under pressure, including during incidents.

Background Information

Contract terms: Open ended contract

Purpose of the Job

The Senior Data Analyst is responsible for managing and optimizing the Bank's hybrid (on-premises and cloud) database and data platform estate, transforming data into actionable insights that drive business objectives. The role covers database design, performance tuning, ETL processes, data modelling, reporting, and analytics in support of core banking and enterprise applications running on both monolithic and microservices architectures. The Senior Data Analyst works closely with the Application Management, Service Management, and IT Infrastructure units to ensure the availability, security, and performance of data platforms, and partners with business stakeholders to define data requirements and deliver reliable, actionable reporting and analytics.

Main Responsibilities of the Job

Duties and responsibilities shall include but not limited to:

A. Data Analysis & Insights

  • Conduct data analysis to identify trends, patterns, and insights that inform business decisions.
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to define data requirements and design data solutions.
  • Design and deliver reliable reports, dashboards, and analytics outputs using data visualization tools.
  • Communicate insights and findings clearly to technical and business stakeholders.

B. Database & Data Platform Management (Hybrid: On-Premises & Cloud)

  • Design, develop, and maintain database structures, data elements, and data models across on-premises and cloud data platforms.
  • Monitor and optimize database performance, including testing, error correction, and troubleshooting of resource-related and performance challenges.
  • Ensure timely and accurate database backups, replication, and high availability for critical systems in a hybrid environment.
  • Implement security measures to protect and secure data across the hybrid database and data platform estate.

C. ETL, Integration & Data-Layer Support

  • Perform data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) processes to ensure data accuracy and integrity.
  • Support the database and data layers of core banking and enterprise applications — spanning monolithic and microservices architectures — including configuration, maintenance, and troubleshooting, in coordination with the Application Management unit.
  • Support the data integration of the Bank's systems, including Electronic Financial Management Information Systems, with external partners.
  • Collaborate with the Application Management and Service Management units to resolve database- and data-related incidents within agreed SLAs.

D. Automation, Scripting & Technical Support

  • Use scripting languages (Bash, Python) and programming skills to automate data manipulation, analysis, and visualization tasks.
  • Provide timely technical support to system users for database- and data-related issues.
  • Participate in process improvement and automation initiatives to enhance operational efficiency across the hybrid data platform.

E. Vendor & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with vendors to review contracts and manage vendor support for database and data platform tools.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional IT teams — Infrastructure, Application Management, and Service Management — on IT projects to deliver efficient solutions.
  • Mentor and support junior data analysts, and stay up to date with emerging trends in data analysis and database/data platform management.

Performance Indicators

  • Accuracy, timeliness, and reliability of data analysis and reporting outputs.
  • Database and data platform availability and performance across on-premises and cloud environments.
  • SLA adherence for database-related incidents and requests.
  • Successful and accurate execution of ETL processes and data integrity checks.
  • Timeliness and success rate of database backups, DR tests, and restores.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and quality of technical support provided.

Working relationships

Internal: Database and Data Platform, Application Management, Service Management, IT Infrastructure, Business Units, Internal Audit.External: Database/data platform vendors, integration partners, core banking application vendors.

Professional, academic qualifications and experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Science, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of experience in data analysis and database management, preferably supporting hybrid (on-premises/cloud) environments.
  • Proficiency in SQL and database management systems (e.g., Oracle, MySQL, SQL Server).
  • Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI).
  • Knowledge of data warehousing concepts and methodologies.
  • Strong understanding of data privacy and security best practices.
  • Relevant certifications in data analysis or database management are an added advantage.

Core competencies

  • Ability to analyze and interpret complex data sets.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks and projects simultaneously.
  • Effective time and organizational management skills.
  • Ability to communicate insights and findings to stakeholders effectively.
  • Continuous learning and adaptability to new technologies and tools.
  • Collaborative mindset with willingness to share knowledge and mentor junior analysts.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.

greatrwandajobs.description:
The University of Rwanda (UR), through the College of Medicine and Health Sciences (CMHS), School of Medicine and Pharmacy, is seeking a qualified and highly motivated Specialist Neurologist to strengthen specialist clinical care, medical education, research, and academic development within its affiliated teaching hospitals.

The Specialist Neurologist will provide high-quality, evidence-based neurological care to inpatients and outpatients while contributing actively to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, clinical supervision, research, mentorship, quality improvement, and professional service.

The successful candidate will work closely with clinical and academic teams to strengthen neurological services and contribute to the training of medical students, interns, residents, postgraduate trainees, and other healthcare professionals.

Responsibilities or duties

  • Provide specialist neurological assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up for patients with a wide range of neurological disorders.
  • Conduct specialist outpatient clinics and provide inpatient neurological consultations.
  • Participate in emergency neurological care, including the management of acute stroke, seizures, altered consciousness, and other neurological emergencies.
  • Request, interpret, and appropriately utilize laboratory, neuroimaging, electrophysiological, and other diagnostic investigations.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment and follow-up plans and make appropriate referrals to multidisciplinary services.
  • Participate in ward rounds, multidisciplinary meetings, case conferences, clinical audits, morbidity and mortality meetings, and other clinical review activities.
  • Maintain accurate, confidential, and timely clinical records in accordance with professional standards and hospital policies.
  • Promote patient safety, ethical practice, evidence-based care, and compliance with applicable clinical guidelines and hospital procedures.
  • Teach medical students, interns, residents, postgraduate trainees, and other healthcare professionals through bedside teaching, lectures, seminars, case presentations, journal clubs, and other appropriate learning activities.
  • Supervise, assess, and mentor trainees in accordance with programme requirements and provide appropriate academic and career guidance.
  • Contribute to the development and review of curricula, clinical guidelines, teaching materials, examinations, and other academic resources.
  • Conduct and supervise clinical and academic research relevant to neurology and institutional health priorities.
  • Publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present research at professional and academic conferences.
  • Promote evidence-based practice and encourage research engagement among residents, medical students, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Participate in departmental and hospital committees, quality improvement initiatives, clinical audits, and on-call services.
  • Contribute to the development and review of departmental policies, protocols, standard operating procedures, and clinical guidelines.
  • Maintain active professional registration, medical licensure, continuing professional development, and other applicable professional requirements.
  • Perform any other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the Programme Director or Head of Department.

Qualifications or requirements

  • Recognized Medical Degree (MD, MBBS, MBChB) from an accredited institution.
  • Recognized postgraduate specialist qualification in Neurology, such as an MMed, Specialist Degree, or Fellowship in Neurology.
  • Valid registration and licence to practice medicine issued by the relevant professional regulatory authority.
  • Eligibility for appointment at Senior Lecturer level or above, in accordance with applicable University of Rwanda academic requirements.
  • For qualifications obtained outside Rwanda, the candidate must provide the required Equivalence Certificate from the Rwanda Higher Education Council (HEC) prior to final appointment.

Experience needed

  • Relevant clinical experience in neurology with demonstrated ability to independently manage neurological patients.
  • Demonstrated experience in teaching, clinical supervision, or mentorship of medical students, interns, residents, or other healthcare professionals.
  • Demonstrated experience in clinical, academic, or research activities relevant to neurology.
  • Strong clinical and diagnostic skills in the assessment and management of neurological conditions.
  • Excellent clinical decision-making and problem-solving abilities.
  • Strong commitment to evidence-based practice, patient safety, and quality clinical care.
  • Demonstrated ability to teach, supervise, mentor, and support the professional development of trainees.
  • Strong research, academic writing, and scientific communication skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, and teamwork skills.
  • Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary clinical and academic teams.
  • High standards of professional ethics, confidentiality, integrity, and accountability.
  • Commitment to continuous professional development and lifelong learning.
  • Ability to contribute effectively to clinical governance, quality improvement, and institutional development.

Why Join This Project?

  • Contribute to the strengthening of specialist neurological services within Rwanda's teaching hospitals.
  • Support the training and development of the next generation of medical doctors and specialist physicians.
  • Participate in clinical research and academic activities addressing national and regional health priorities.
  • Work within a multidisciplinary academic and clinical environment.
  • Contribute to evidence-based improvements in neurological care, medical education, and health service delivery.

greatrwandajobs.title: Gender-Transformative & Social Inclusion Expert (GTSI) (H/F) job at Expertise France
greatrwandajobs.description:
Expertise France is the French public agency for international technical cooperation. Present in over 100 countries, the agency engineers and implements capacity-building projects, mobilizes technical expertise, and acts as project coordinator across four priority areas: democratic, economic and financial governance; stability in crisis and post-crisis contexts; climate change and sustainable urban development; and strengthening health systems, social protection and employment. About TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” is on of Expertise France projects that is being implemented in Rwanda. The “TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” project aims to contribute to the National Strategy for Transformation and Vision 2050 established by the Government of Rwanda to guide the socio-economic development of the country towards a prosperous and high-income economy by 2050. Representing 25% of GDP and 70% of Rwanda's active population, agriculture is a key sector targeted in order to boost the country's economy and create jobs is one of the priorities for the sector's transformation, with the national objective of establishing TVET Centers of Excellence in Agriculture (CoE, also referred to as Centers of Vocational Excellence).

The “TVET Agri – Ubuhinzi Skills+” project is implemented by Expertise France to support the national agency Rwanda TVET Board (RTB) in the establishment of TVET Centers of Excellence in Agriculture. In line with national priorities, the project aims to increase the sustainability, climate resilience and inclusion of agricultural practices by strengthening the skills of women and youth in Rwanda.

The project is structured around two specific objectives:

  • Improve access of women and youth to quality skills and formal certification in agricultural practices.
  • Improve the effectiveness of mechanisms for integrating women and young people into the agricultural labor market, with an emphasis on sustainable agriculture.

In Rwanda, 77% of farmers are women, mainly in subsistence agriculture, vulnerable to climate change. The project is classified under the OECD-DAC Gender Equality Policy Marker 2: gender equality is a principal objective of the intervention, and the project implements transformative and sustainable actions for women, young girls and their communities.

The project is implemented over a period of five years, with a budget of +16 million euros financed by the EU and the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. It includes technical assistance at the national level in support of RTB, and two Technical Secondary Schools — Kisaro TSS (Rulindo District) and AEF Nyagahanga (Gatsibo District) — are also supported with technical assistance, infrastructure rehabilitation and procurement of agricultural equipment as they transform into Agricultural TVET Centers of Excellence. The project is implemented in collaboration with the beneficiary partner RTB, as well as with donors and project partners, such as LuxDev.

The project is led by the Project Manager, with direct support from the Deputy Project Manager, and the team consists of 4 Technical Experts, a MEAL Officer, and 2 Project Advisors based in targeted TVET schools. The team is supported by Expertise France's Kigali-based Project Support Unit (PSU) for administration, finance, Human Resources and procurement, as well as Paris-based HQ.

The project has adopted and validated a Gender-Transformative and Socially Inclusive Framework Strategy (2024–2029) , with an accompanying Training Architecture and a detailed, DAC-aligned Action Plan. The project is now entering its transition phase — running for a minimum of three years — during which this strategy moves from formulation to full institutional implementation across both Centers of Excellence. This phase places substantially higher technical and delivery demands on the position than the project's start-up year.

Responsibilities or duties

1. To lead the implementation of the Gender-Transformative Framework Strategy

Operate the Theory of Change. Drive the five transformation pathways — inclusive governance; equitable and safe learning environments; gender-responsive work-based learning; safeguarding and GBV prevention; inclusive transition to employment and entrepreneurship — as a single integrated system, advancing them in parallel rather than as isolated activities.

Translate strategy into delivery. Convert the strategy’s Action Plan into detailed annual and quarterly operational programming: sequencing, responsibilities, milestones, budget lines and monitoring calendars, fully reflected in project workplans.

Secure OECD-DAC Marker 2 compliance. Lead the classification, indicator design (DAC 1 & 2 aligned, sex-, age- and disability-disaggregated), evidence base and EU reporting required to sustain the project’s Marker 2 status, in liaison with the MEAL Officer.

Provide technical direction across the team. Guide the other Technical Experts, Project Advisors and RTB counterparts so that gender-transformative and inclusion requirements are embedded in curricula, work-based learning, infrastructure design, procurement specifications and terms of reference across all workstreams — not carried by the GTSI workstream alone. Lead the GTSI Technical Working Group.

2. To design and deliver advanced capacity-building content

Author high-level training material. Personally design, write and quality-assure competency-based training content, facilitator guides, participant handbooks, audit tools and assessment instruments across all levels of the project’s Training Architecture. The authorship of this material is a core deliverable of the post.

Deliver and certify. Facilitate or co-facilitate training for school teachers and leadership, project and RTB staff, private-sector work-based learning host companies, and students; operate the associated certification and recognition framework with RTB.

Engage beyond the schools. Develop and implement the engagement approach for private-sector actors, cooperatives, farmers and adult learners, including Inclusion Compacts, employer awareness sessions and workplace inclusion standards.

Build sustainable learning systems. Establish and animate Communities of Practice so that gender and inclusion competency is sustained beyond direct project interventions.

3. To manage the GTSI activity package end to end

Programme and deliver. Own operational planning, sequencing and delivery of the full GTSI activity package to the standard set by the Action Plan.

Manage procurement and consultants. Prepare terms of reference, contribute to procurement in liaison with the PSU, and technically supervise national and international consultants mobilised on GTSI assignments, including quality control and technical validation of their deliverables.

Manage the budget. Plan, propose and track GTSI budget lines, including gender-responsive budgeting, ensuring sound execution and donor compliance.

Monitor, evaluate and report. Track progress against disaggregated indicators, capture lessons learned, operate the GTSI dashboard/MIS in liaison with the MEAL Officer, and report to project leadership, RTB and the donor.

4. To support the transition of the schools into TVET Centres of Excellence in Agriculture

Institutionalise the gender-transformative agenda. Support Kisaro TSS and AEF Nyagahanga to embed gender equality and social inclusion in governance, planning, budgeting, staff performance frameworks and accountability systems, including scorecards and community accountability forums.

Secure inclusive access to practice. Operationalise measures ensuring equitable access for female learners and learners with disabilities to practical training units, dual training and internships, including the control points needed to counter guidance bias and de facto exclusion.

Institutionalise safe learning environments. Support the establishment of GBV/SEAH reporting mechanisms, accessible grievance channels and safeguarding referral pathways aligned with PSEA standards.

Promote inclusive campuses. Provide technical inputs during design, construction and renovation so that facilities are accessible to women, persons with disabilities and other disadvantaged groups.

Qualifications or requirements

Master’s Degree in Gender and Development, Social Inclusion, Development Studies, Sociology or another relevant field.

Experience needed

At least 10 years of progressive professional experience in gender equality and social inclusion within development programmes.

Demonstrable experience of gender-transformative programming — that is, work explicitly aimed at changing institutional norms, structures and power relations — as distinct from gender mainstreaming, gender analysis, gender audits or awareness-raising.

Proven experience translating a gender-transformative strategy, theory of change or action plan into multi-year operational implementation down to activity level, within a single institutional system.

Demonstrated experience personally authoring and delivering advanced, competency-based training content for institutional audiences (teachers, management, technical staff) and private-sector actors.

Direct experience of OECD-DAC Gender Equality Policy Marker 2 and/or EU GAP III compliance, indicator design and donor reporting is strongly desirable.

Solid project-management experience embedded within an implementation team: operational planning, procurement, technical supervision of consultants, budget execution and monitoring of an activity package.

Experience providing technical direction to multidisciplinary teams of senior experts, and coordinating multi-stakeholder initiatives with government, private-sector, civil-society and academic partners.

Skills

Technical authorship. Ability to independently produce strategies, theories of change, action plans, guidance notes and training curricula of a standard suitable for donor and institutional validation.

Gender-transformative methodologies. Command of norm-change approaches, intersectionality, the Human Rights-Based Approach and Leave No One Behind, and their practical application to institutional transformation.

Understanding of TVET and agriculture sector challenges. Familiarity with labour market dynamics and skills development, especially for women and youth.

Disability inclusion, safeguarding and PSEA. GBV/SEAH mechanisms, Universal Design for Learning and accessibility standards.

Activity and budget management. Operational planning, procurement, consultant follow-up, gender-responsive budgeting and budget execution.

Communication, facilitation and advocacy. Ability to design and deliver technical presentations and facilitation before institutional partners, donors and private-sector audiences.

Initiative and autonomy. Capacity to identify needs, formulate approaches and produce deliverables without close supervision.

Digital literacy. Proficiency in standard office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

Language proficiency. Excellent written and spoken command of English — the working language with the donor, RTB and partners — and of Kinyarwanda; French is an asset.

Any other provided details

Why Join Expertise France?

  • Contribute to a high-impact regional program shaping Africa's digital future.
  • Work alongside leading African and European institutions and experts.
  • Gain exposure to complex multi-country and multi-donor program management.
  • Develop your professional expertise within a recognized international organization.
  • Be part of a collaborative, multicultural, and inclusive working environment.
